zh: 第二章　论弑河
en: 2 On Rivercide

zh: 十九世纪的埃及为了信用货币的生产和偿还，经历了一场地理与生态的灾难性重排。这场灾难使我们得以更仔细地考察殖民占领、生态破坏与对未来进行资本化攫取之间的联系。埃及或许比世界上任何其他地方都更能体现货币生钱的力量。约瑟夫·熊彼特利用他在开罗的短暂经历，发展出把资本主义解释为“创造性破坏”的理论；这种对资本主义现代性的理解至今仍塑造着人们的想象方式。熊彼特为这种破坏性创造力提供的少数具体例子之一，就来自他对埃及农业转型的短暂参与。但那场破坏究竟包括什么？需要怎样重排技术圈？它又建立在怎样的未来生产、过去重想、技术诀窍重组、托词安排和无知扩张之上？
en: Egypt in the nineteenth century endured a catastrophic reordering of its geography and ecology in the service of the production and repayment of credit. The catastrophe allows us to look more closely at the connection between colonial occupation, ecological destruction, and the capitalising capture of the future. Egypt became a place, perhaps more than any other site in the world, that exemplified the power of money to make money. Joseph Schumpeter used his brief experience in Cairo to develop an explanation of capitalism as ‘creative destruction’, an understanding of capitalist modernity that still shapes the way it is imagined today. One of the few concrete examples that Schumpeter offered of this destructive creativity was drawn from his brief involvement in the agricultural transformation of Egypt. But what exactly did that destruction involve? What reordering of the technosphere was required? And on what producing of the future, reimagining of the past, reorganisation of know-how, arranging of alibis, and expansion of ignorance would it be based?

zh: “每位水利工程师都自认为是金融家，”威廉·威尔科克斯在回顾自己在埃及的职业生涯时写道，“而每位金融家都自认为是水利工程师。”
威尔科克斯制定了阿斯旺大坝——建于 1899—1902 年——的第一批设计方案，后来管理了建坝出资人——英国资本家和企业家欧内斯特·卡塞尔爵士——的糖业地产。正如我们所见，正是卡塞尔糖业投资的崩溃把熊彼特带到了开罗。在埃及，水利工程是一种新金融秩序的基础，而这一秩序又得益于新程度的创造性破坏。信用创造、从未来
抽吸支付的装置，不仅由欧内斯特·卡塞尔及其合伙人欧内斯特·克罗尼耶这样的企业家建造，也由运河、水闸、大坝、拦河堰和蒸汽泵构成。从未来获取，反过来又需要重写过去。
en: ‘Every hydraulic engineer considered himself a financier’, wrote William Willcocks, reflecting on his career in Egypt, ‘and every financier considered himself a hydraulic engineer.’

Willcocks produced the first designs for the Aswan Dam, built in 1899–1902, and later managed the sugar estates of the man who financed it, the English capitalist and entrepreneur Sir Ernest Cassel. It was the collapse of Cassel’s sugar investments, as we saw, that had brought Schumpeter to Cairo. In Egypt, hydraulic engineering was the basis of a new financial order, enabled by a new degree of creative destruction. The apparatus of credit creation, of

the suction of payments from the future, was being built not just by entrepreneurs like Ernest Cassel and his partner Ernest Cronier, but out of canals, sluices, dams, barrages, and steam pumps. The acquisition from the future would require, in turn, a rewriting of the past.

zh: 1882 年，英国为应对一场政治—金融危机而占领埃及。欧洲银行家运用其扩张的信用创造工具，相继发行政府贷款，每一笔贷款都确立了对不同未来收入来源的控制。各省税收、国家铁路、盐税、关税，以及最终统治者私人种植园，依次被抵押给银行家。每笔新贷款中越来越大的部分，用于偿还先前债务的利息和费用。

每一笔贷款都把未来收入流的耐久性，与把那些预期收入之控制权转化为当下信用支付的安排的流动性结合起来。1873 年的国际金融危机由欧洲和美国铁路股票投机崩溃引发，并导致全球性萧条；加上再没有公共收入可供抵押，埃及政府被迫破产。一场反对政权及其债权人的民众起义导致了民族主义政府的建立，并使该国最大的地主和金融家寻求外部支持以恢复旧秩序，从而促成了英国的军事占领。1884 年，另一场民众起义的成功——马赫迪派推翻苏丹的埃及统治——以及开罗的又一轮金融危机，说服英国把临时的“干预”变成一种不设期限的帝国行政。
en: The British had occupied Egypt in 1882 in response to a political-financial crisis. European bankers had deployed their expanded tools of credit creation to float successive government loans, each establishing a hold over a different source of future revenue. The taxes of individual provinces, the state railways, the salt tax, customs duties, and eventually the ruler’s private plantations were each mortgaged in turn to the bankers. An increasing part of every new loan was devoted to repaying interest and fees on the previous debts.

Each loan combined the durability of a future flow of income with the liquidity of the arrangement that converted the control of those prospective revenues into a credit payment in the present. The international financial crisis of 1873, precipitated by the collapse of speculation in railway shares in Europe and the United States and leading to a worldwide depression, along with the lack of any further public revenues to mortgage, forced the Egyptian government into bankruptcy. A popular revolt against the regime and its creditors led to the creation of a nationalist government and caused the country’s largest landowners and financiers to seek external support to restore the old order, precipitating Britain’s military occupation. In 1884, the success of another popular revolt – the Mahdist overthrow of Egyptian rule in Sudan – and another round of financial crisis in Cairo persuaded Britain to turn its temporary ‘intervention’ into an open-ended imperial administration.

zh: 反复无常的自然
en: A Volatile Nature

zh: 随后是长达五十年、把一个国家改造成偿债机器的实验。建造这台机器既需要水利工程师调节世界最长河流的水流，也需要历史学家重写世界上有记载的最长历史之一。要理解这台机器的运作，必须重新考虑英国如何通过重新工程化尼罗河建立殖民政权的标准叙述。
en: There followed a five-decade experiment in remaking a country as a repayment machine. The building of this machine required both the work of irrigation engineers to alter the flow of the world’s longest river and the work of historians to rewrite one of the world’s longest recorded histories. To understand the working of this machine, the standard account of how Britain built a colonial regime through the re-engineering of the Nile needs to be reconsidered.

zh: 这种标准叙述几乎立即开始被书写。1890 年，我们
在上一章匆匆提到过的美国工程师戴维·埃姆斯·韦尔斯，出版了后来成为该时期美国最有影响的经济学文本的著作。他把埃及的转型置于他对 1870 年代以来技术创新所引发的革命性“扰动”的论述中心，预见了二十年后熊彼特的思想。他从苏伊士运河的例子开始，以英国工程师对尼罗河的改造结束。
en: The standard account began to be written almost immediately. In 1890 the American engineer David Ames Wells, whom we met in

passing in the previous chapter, published what was to become the most influential US economic text of the period. He placed the transformation of Egypt at the centre of his account of the revolutionary ‘disturbances’ brought on by technical innovation since the 1870s, anticipating the ideas of Schumpeter two decades later. He started with the example of the Suez Canal and ended with the transformation of the Nile by the work of British engineers.

zh: 1884 年，英国实际上占有了埃及；从那一刻起，在一群熟练工程师和实干者的管理下，这个国家赖以维持人民生命与繁荣的供水和灌溉系统开始了一场革新，并且已经带来了极其仁慈的结果。在下埃及，土地开垦正以每年五万英亩的速度进行，在尼罗河谷其他地区则达到这一数字的两倍；这为一个备受压迫、贫穷困苦的种族提供了数百年未有的更好机会，使他们能用自己的劳动养活自己。
en: In 1884 Britain virtually took possession of Egypt, and from that moment there was initiated, under the management of a body of skilled engineers and practical men, a renovation of the water-supply and irrigation system of the country upon which the life and prosperity of its people depend, and which has already been attended with results of extraordinary beneficence. In Lower Egypt land reclamation is going on at the rate of fifty thousand acres per annum, and in other sections of the Nile Valley at double that amount; giving to a down-trodden and impoverished race better opportunities than they have had for centuries of supporting themselves by their own labor.

zh: 按照传统叙述，英国最早采取的步骤之一，是废除旧农业制度所依赖的所谓“传统”强制劳动制度——
（徭役）。
接着，占领当局处理埃及农业发展长期面临的问题——反复无常的自然力量。“埃及的历史就是人类利用尼罗河的故事，”后来成为现代埃及主要经济史著作的作者写道，“如果放任不管，这条河将是一位反复无常、变化多端的女主人，今年带来繁荣，明年带来饥荒。自从人类在尼罗河谷定居以来，就一直在以不同程度的成功努力驯服这条河，使它为自己服务。”
我们将会发现，这段关于反复无常、不确定性和饥荒的历史是编造出来的。
en: One of Britain’s first steps, the conventional story goes, was to abolish the so-called ‘traditional’ system of forced labour, the
, on which the old agrarian system was based.

Next, the occupying authorities addressed the persistent problem facing the development of agriculture in Egypt – the volatile forces of nature. ‘The history of Egypt is the story of the use man has made of the Nile’, wrote the author of what became the leading economic history of modern Egypt. ‘Left to herself, the river would be a capricious and changeful mistress, bringing prosperity one year, famine the next. Ever since man settled down in the Nile Valley, he has endeavoured, with the varying degrees of success, to tame the river and turn it to his service.’
This history of volatility, uncertainty, and famine, as we will discover, was a fabrication.

zh: 一切耕作都依赖河流每年的泛滥，而历史学家声称，泛滥的范围无法预测。为了矫正这一点，英国人设计了一套他们称为“洪水控制”的新系统，以调节河流的水流。
首先，他们监督修复开罗以北的一座拦河堰，提高河流向尼罗河三角洲主要运河供水处的水位。随后，他们在南方的阿斯旺修建了一座大得多的水坝，并在前两者中间、艾斯尤特修建了第三座拦河堰。这些工程使尼罗河水能够储存在坝后水库中，调节

夏季每年的泛滥，并把大部分灌溉系统从围堤田块改造为永久运河。据说，新的蓄水机制提高了农业生产力，办法是把全国大部分农业从每年一季、在洪水退去后的围堤田块播种的制度，转变为常年种植制度，同一块田每年可种两三季作物。尼罗河三角洲许多地区和中埃及的小块地区已经引入常年种植，通过畜力灌溉机械，以及日益增多的蒸汽泵，从河流或本世纪早些时候修建的深运河中提水。新的拦河堰运作方式不同：它们不是加深运河以便在河流水位低时输水，而是在全年提高河流和运河的水位，使该国四分之三以上的农田得以从围堤田块的季节性利用转变为全年种植。这反过来又使棉花和甘蔗这两种主要工业作物的生产大规模扩张。用于出口的棉花种植面积，在 1820 年代和 1830 年代有限水平的基础上，到 1860 年代和 1870 年代已增至十倍，1882 年后的二十年里又翻了一倍多。
据标准叙述，棉花种植成为该国经济增长的支柱，并把它整合进所谓的世界市场。
en: All cultivation depended on the annual inundation of the river, whose extent, historians claimed, was unpredictable. To remedy this, the British engineered a new system of what they termed ‘flood control’ to alter the flow of the river.

First, they supervised repairs to a barrage north of Cairo, raising the level of the river where it supplied the main canals of the Nile Delta. They then built the much larger dam in the south at Aswan, together with a third barrage midway between the other two, at Asyut. These made it possible to store the water of the Nile in the reservoir behind the dam, regulate the annual inundation in the

summer, and convert most of the irrigation system from flood basins to permanent canals. The new storage mechanisms allowed an increase in agricultural productivity, it was said, by switching most of the country’s agriculture from a system based on a single annual crop, sown in the catch basins after the flood waters receded, to a system of perennial cultivation, in which two or three crops a year could be grown in the same field. Many parts of the Nile Delta and small areas of Middle Egypt had already introduced perennial cropping, lifting water from the river or deep-lying canals constructed earlier in the century, via animalpowered irrigation machines and, increasingly, steam pumps. The new barrages worked differently: rather than deepening the canals to carry water when the river was low, they raised the water level in the river and the canals throughout the year, allowing the conversion of more than three-quarters of the country’s fields from the seasonal use of flood basins to year-round cultivation. This in turn enabled a large expansion in the production of the two main industrial crops, cotton and sugar cane. The area devoted to growing cotton for export, which had already increased tenfold by the 1860s and 1870s from its modest levels in the 1820s and 1830s, more than doubled again in the two decades after 1882.
Its cultivation became the mainstay of the country’s economic growth, according to standard accounts, and integrated it into so-called world markets.

zh: 因此，埃及的历史被讲述为与自然的遭遇，其形式是一条河流，而这条河流不可预测的洪水使她成为一位需要被“驯服”的“反复无常、变化多端的女主人”。负责驯服她的人掌握了调节和管理她反复无常的技术手段。关于如何管理未驯服的社会力量，也有一种平行的论述。
，连同
——用埃及河马的皮制成、用来强制执行强制劳动制度的鞭子（甚至当河马正被其皮所强制推行的灌溉工程逼向灭绝时也是如此）——集中体现了一个腐败专制的政府，而它将被改造为法治而人道的政府。
正如自然力量将被控制，东方天然的专制将被一种更理性、更人道的行政所取代。在这种叙述中，技术重组的作用是改善、推进、合理化并提高生产力。
en: Thus, the history of Egypt is told as the encounter with nature, in the form of a river whose unpredictable flood made her a ‘capricious and changeful mistress’ in need of being ‘tamed’. The men taking charge of her taming had mastered the technical means to regulate and manage her capriciousness. A parallel argument was made about the administering of untamed social forces. The
, together with the

, the whip made from the hide of the Egyptian hippo and used to enforce the compulsory labour regime (even as the hippo was being driven extinct by the very irrigation works its hide enforced), epitomised a corrupt and despotic government that was to be rendered juridical and humane.

Just as the forces of nature were to be controlled, the natural despotism of the East was to be replaced with a more rational, more humane, administration. The role of technical reorganisation, in this account, was to improve, to advance, to rationalise, and to make more productive.

zh: 当焦点不在于从未驯服的自然（无论是物理的还是人类的）中安排、改良和榨取剩余的问题，而在于如何通过灌溉工程
建造技术圈，把它变成攫取未来的新装置时，这段历史就呈现为不同的样子。

我们不应假定技术变化就是改良，而应追问问题是怎样被定义的，解决方案又服务于什么。十九世纪埃及农民面临的主要威胁，不是尼罗河洪水过高或过低的问题。那种“风险”很容易被夸大，而工程本身又使它更加严重。农民面临一种不同的、反复出现的生态威胁，它正是近来毁灭性作物歉收和经济灾难的原因。它还可能增加了过度泛滥的概率。这种新威胁影响了现有的安排：把多余的尼罗河水储存起来，供泛滥退去、洪泛平原排干之后使用；这种安排使耕作者能够应对洪水过高过低的问题，但如今却要被摧毁。
en: This history appears differently when the focus is placed not on the problems of ordering, improving, and extracting a surplus from an untamed nature (whether physical or human), but on how the making
of a technosphere built out of irrigation works a new apparatus for the capture of the future.

We should not assume that technical changes were improvements, but ask how the problems were defined and for what the solutions were useful. The main threat faced by Egyptian farmers in the nineteenth century was not the problem of high and low Nile floods. That ‘risk’ was easily exaggerated and the engineering works themselves made it worse. Farmers faced a different, recurrent ecological threat, one that was the cause of recent, devastating crop failures and economic calamity. It may also have increased the likelihood of excessive inundation. The new threat affected an existing arrangement for storing surplus Nile waters for use after the inundation and draining of the floodplain, an arrangement that allowed cultivators to manage the problem of high and low floods, but which was now to be destroyed.

zh: 与本世纪早些时候进行的灌溉工程不同，英国建造的蓄水系统没有承认现有机制，没有考虑其长处，也没有处理这些其他脆弱性。新安排处理的不是那些问题，而是资本化问题：如何把田地从产生和储存财富、只允许有限形式信用创造的安排，转变为一种从未来产生预期收入流的装置，这些收入流可以在当下变现，成为那些在空间和时间上都与田地分离者的非劳动所得。这一切都不是由对棉花或糖等原料的特定
所驱动，也不是由欧洲“剩余”资本的流动所驱动，也不是由把埃及在空间上整合进世界市场的需求所驱动。那些都是常见的故事。它也不代表十九世纪晚期金融化的新阶段，因为至少从本世纪中叶起，创造信用并从信用建设中获利，一直是欧洲参与灌溉和农业计划的目的，而在此前很久，参与贸易计划也是如此。
en: Unlike the irrigation works carried out earlier in the century, the storage system built by the British did not recognise the existing mechanism, did not consider its strengths, and did not deal with these other vulnerabilities. The new arrangement addressed not those issues, but the problem of capitalisation: how to convert the fields from arrangements that produced and stored wealth, allowing only limited forms of credit creation, into an apparatus producing flows of prospective revenue from the future, which could be realised in the present and made into unearned income for those separated from the fields in both space and time. None of this was driven by a particular

for raw materials, such as cotton or sugar, nor by a flow of ‘surplus’ capital from Europe, nor by a demand to integrate Egypt spatially into a world market. Those are the usual stories. Nor did it represent a new, late-nineteenth-century stage of financialisation, for the creating and profiting from credit construction had been the purpose of European involvement in irrigation and agricultural schemes since at least the middle of the century, and in trading schemes long before that.

zh: 水车会吱呀作响吗？
en: Can the Waterwheel Squeak?

zh: 1990 年代及其后二十年，我曾多次在埃及南部一个村庄生活，了解人们如何耕种土地、维持生计。我们住的房子旁边，靠着一堵畜棚的土坯墙，立着一台拆散的木质灌溉机械——一个巨大的带齿木轮，属于

，即畜力水车。我得知，这台机器曾被用来从一口井里提水，灌溉周围的田地；那口井就挖在我们现在房子所在地的旁边。与我同龄的男人记得年轻时在 1960 年代末阿斯旺高坝完工之前帮忙操作水车。我从年长的男人那里了解到一件不同寻常的事。在大坝建成前的旧日里，每年洪水退去后，这样的水车会被架设在田野各处，每一台都安放在一个砖砌的大型地下蓄水池或水井上。这些水井和水车构成了一个广泛的蓄水和灌溉农业系统，而我从未读到过。
甚至三十年后，这种蓄水方式以及它所组织的世界，仍从未被描述过。
en: During the 1990s and over the following two decades, I lived for several periods in a village in the south of Egypt, learning how people farmed the land and made their livelihoods. Next to the house where we lived, against the mudbrick wall of an animal shelter, stood the disassembled parts of a wooden irrigation machine – the large, toothed wheel of a

, or animal-driven waterwheel. The machine, I learned, was once used to raise water from a well that had been dug adjacent to where our house now stood, to irrigate the surrounding field. The men of my age remembered helping with the wheel in their youth, before the completion of the High Dam at Aswan in the late 1960s. From older men I learned something remarkable. In the old days before the dam, once the flood waters receded each year, waterwheels like this would be assembled across the fields, each one placed over a large, brick-built underground cistern or well. The wells and waterwheels constituted an extensive system of water storage and irrigated farming about which I had never read.
Even today, thirty years later, this method of storage, and the world it organised, has never been described.

zh: 储存问题对我们思考资本主义的方式很重要。在许多论述中，前现代国家通过控制储存来治理。开罗等城市的大型粮仓可以充当政府税收支付的接收者、信用机制和价格控制工具。它还可以在短缺时期供应粮食，以防混乱。据说，在资本主义下，储存被转变为一种组织流动和人口控制的不同方法。大多数商品可以通过市场交换按需获得，因此现在只有某些战略物品被储存，主要是那些具有液态或流动形式的东西——水、石油，尤其是货币。

其中最大的货币资本，被想象为从过去积累起来的储备，但储存起来就会贬值。它必须被迅速投入运转并分散开来，以补充储备，实际上扩大储备。因此，大多数关于资本主义的论述实际上保留了一种简单的储存模式：从过去堆积起来的东西支配未来。我们在此探索一种不同的理解：资本是攫取或资产化未来的装置，使少数人能够在当下享用那种未来收入，并把随后偿还的负担强加给多数人。从未来获取不仅通过金融工程运作，也通过工业生活、人类生计和生态系统的工程运作。埃及的蓄水和水利工程史可以提供一种关于资本主义现代性的不同叙述。储存既没有消失，也没有增加。它被重组到新的手中，转移到新的地点，在运作上被大幅简化。这场改变地球的转型，摧毁了河流本身的生命，其目的不是储存储备，而是构造对未来的新支配。
en: The question of storage is important to how we think about capitalism. In many accounts, pre-modern states governed through the control of storage. A large grain store in a city such as Cairo could serve as the recipient of government tax payments, a machinery of credit, and an instrument of price control. It could also be used to prevent disorder, by supplying grain in periods of shortage. Under capitalism, it is said, storage was transformed into a different method of organising the control of flows and populations. Most goods could be acquired on demand through market exchange, so now only certain strategic items were stored, mainly those available in liquid form – water, petroleum, and above all money.

The largest of these, money capital, is imagined as a reserve accumulated from the past, but one that loses value if stored. It must be quickly put in motion and dispersed, to replenish the store and indeed expand it. So, most accounts of capitalism in fact retain a simple storage model: what is piled up from the past governs the future. Here we are exploring a different understanding: capital as apparatuses that capture, or assetise, the future, allowing a few to enjoy that future income in the present and imposing on the majority the burden of its subsequent repayment. The acquisition from the future operates not only through financial engineering, but through the engineering of industrial life, human livelihoods, and ecological systems. The history of water storage and hydraulic engineering in Egypt can offer a different account of capitalist modernity. Storage neither disappeared nor increased. It was reorganised into new hands, relocated in new locations, and vastly simplified in operation. This terraforming transformation, in which the very life of the river was destroyed, was to serve not the storing up of a reserve but the constructing of a new command of the future.

zh: 对英国人而言，灌溉工程处理的是可见、可测量之物。它忽视无法直接看到和计算的东西。殖民工程师运用水文学——即关于地表水流的科学——来处理尼罗河。他们很少关注后来所谓的水文地质学，即处理不可见、不可测量的地下水。
这种忽视源于无知的制造（agnotology），而非单纯的不知情。他们知道地下水存在，而且正如我们将看到的，它被广泛使用，但他们选择忽视它。
通过估算可见、易于测量和控制的东西——河流或运河横截面的面积及其水流速度——他们能够计算流量，即单位时间内的水量。流量使他们能够估算“单位供水的灌溉面积”（duty of water）；这个术语源于英国用水力驱动机器进行工业生产的用法，后来被印度和埃及的灌溉工程师采用，用以计算给定地表水供应可灌溉的作物面积。
目标是让“尼罗河供水……发挥其能提供的最大功效”。
en: For the British, irrigation engineering dealt with what was visible and measurable. It ignored what could not be directly seen and calculated. Colonial engineers addressed the Nile using the science of hydrology: in terms of the flow of surface water. They paid little attention to what would later be known as hydrogeology, dealing with water that was not visible or measurable, stored beneath the surface.
This inattention was the product of agnotology, not ignorance. They knew that water was present beneath the ground and, as we will see, widely used, but chose to ignore it.

By estimating what could be seen and easily measured and controlled – the area of a cross-section of a river channel or canal and the velocity at which its water moved – they were able to calculate the flow rate, or the volume per unit of time. The flow rate allowed them to estimate the ‘duty of water’, a term coined in the use of water power to run industrial machinery in Britain but taken up by irrigation engineers in India and then Egypt to calculate the area of each crop that a given supply of surface water could irrigate.
The aim was to make ‘the Nile supply . . . do the maximum work that could be got out of it’.

zh: 要理解发生的转变，我们需要以不同方式思考尼罗河，同时考虑可见和不可见的水，从而看到另一种生态。历史学家把先前的安排称为围堤蓄水灌溉，但只提到这个系统的一半。没有任何现代学术研究描述过农民如何把河流用作全年蓄水系统，支撑常年灌溉和多季作物。
英国为拦蓄尼罗河水而修建的大坝，并未引入河水储存，也没有开创常年灌溉和全年农业。相反，它们以不同的、效率更低的方式，把水储存在地表的狭窄河道中。工程师们启动的不是常年灌溉，而是把水截留在地表，而此前水是分散储存于地下的。
en: To understand the transformation that occurred, we need to consider the Nile differently, in terms of both visible and invisible water, bringing into view a different ecology. Historians refer to the previous arrangement as basin irrigation but mention only one-half of the system. No modern scholarship has described how farmers used the river as a year-round storage system, supporting perennial irrigation and multiple crop seasons.

The dams built by the British to impound the Nile did not introduce the storing of its waters and did not initiate perennial irrigation and year-round agriculture. Rather, they stored the waters differently, and less effectively, in a narrow channel on the surface. The engineers instigated, not perennial irrigation, but a trapping of waters on the surface of the land, where they had previously been dispersed and stored beneath it.

zh: 尼罗河谷呈下坡走向，既有纵向的（像所有河流一样），在这里是向北流向地中海，也有横向的：河流的洪泛平原在离河最近处最高，即紧邻主河道的天然堤上。几千年来，河流在夏末因埃塞俄比亚季风雨而上涨，溢出河岸，沉积一层淤泥，它先把最重的淤泥颗粒丢在离河道最近处，形成一道高于洪泛平原其余部分的河岸高台，如图一所示。天然堤之外，土地向外侧倾斜，直到可耕种河谷边缘，止于沙漠的石灰岩陡崖。
en: The Nile Valley runs downhill, both longitudinally (like all rivers), in this case northwards towards the Mediterranean Sea, but also laterally: the floodplain of the river is highest at the point closest to the river, on the levees adjacent to the main channel. Over millennia, as the river, swollen in late summer by the monsoon rains of Ethiopia, overflowed its banks and deposited a layer of silt, it dropped the heaviest particles of silt first, closest to the channel, creating a berm higher than the rest of the floodplain, as shown in figure one. Beyond the levees the land slopes downwards towards the outer edges of the cultivable valley, which ends at the limestone escarpment of the desert.

zh: 围堤蓄水灌溉方法已使用了数千年，经历了发展、废弃和恢复的时期。
在这种制度下，主要灌溉渠道穿过河岸高台，把夏季泛滥的水引到远处的田地。土堤把洪泛平原分成大型蓄水田区，每块一千到数万英亩，又由较小的坝分成便于管理的区块。水闸门或堤坝上的临时开口，使每个田区能够依次蓄水到一到三米深，把富含养分的洪水储存约四十五天，然后把多余的水排入下游较低的田区，最终回到河中。
在 1805 年至 1848 年统治的穆罕默德·阿里治下，工程师改进了蓄水田区的布局，改进了较高与较低田区之间的依次衔接，并增建运河，从更上游引来洪水，供应靠近河流的河岸高地上的田地。
排干洪水后，随着地面开始干燥开裂，农民播种两种主要谷类作物：小麦供富裕者制作面包，大麦用于制作普通面包、喂养马匹和酿造啤酒（尼罗河洪水较弱时，人们更偏好大麦，因为它所需生长季更短、用水更少）。
他们用同样的方法种植豆科作物，主要是喂养牛和水牛的三叶草，以及小扁豆、鹰嘴豆、葫芦巴、羽扇豆和蚕豆。与谷类作物不同，豆科作物为土壤增添更多养分，与
根区吸收空气中氮气并将其转化为可用形态的细菌共生。水、空气、淤泥、土壤、细菌和人类劳动相互作用，生产出这些作物，既不需要人造肥料或额外灌溉，甚至不需要犁地、清除石块、防治害虫或除草的劳动。
en: The method of basin irrigation had been in use for millennia, through periods of development, disuse, and restoration.

Under this system, the main irrigation channels were cut through the berm to carry the summer inundation to the fields beyond. Earthen dykes divided the floodplain into large catch basins, each of a thousand to tens of thousands of acres, subdivided by smaller dams into manageable sections. Sluice gates or temporary openings in the dykes and dams made it possible to fill each basin in turn to a depth of one to three metres, store the nutrient-rich inundation for about forty-five days, and then release the surplus into a lower basin downstream and eventually back into the river.

Under Muhammad Ali, who ruled from 1805 to 1848, engineers had improved the arrangement of catch basins, enhancing the sequence of upper and lower basins and adding canals drawing flood water from further upstream to supply the elevated fields on the berm close to the river.

After draining the flood waters, as the ground began to dry and crack, farmers sowed the two main cereal crops, wheat for the bread of the well-to-do and barley to make ordinary bread and to feed horses and make beer (barley was preferred to wheat when the Nile flood was weak, as it required a shorter growing season and less water).

They used the same method for the leguminous crops, principally clover to feed cattle and water buffalo, alongside lentils, chickpeas, fenugreek, lupins, and broad beans. Unlike the cereal crops, the legumes added further nutrients to the soil, working symbiotically with bacteria in the

root zone that absorb nitrogen from the air and process it into useable form. The interaction of water, air, silt, soil, bacteria, and human labour produced these crops without need for artificial fertiliser or further irrigation, nor even for the labour of ploughing, stone removal, pest control, or weeding.

zh: 每一部埃及农业史都描述这个系统。但还有第二种蓄水方法，用来在冬季主收成之后的初夏生产第二季作物——甚至在秋季生产第三季作物。
穆罕默德·阿里治下引入的改良，部分就是为了加强这种安排。
水不是储存在围堤田块中，而是储存在它们之下的地层中。现代历史学家被殖民灌溉工程师说服，认为旧制度每年只允许种植一季主要作物，“一年其余时间因缺乏灌溉用水而休耕”，因此从未描述过十九世纪后期灌溉方案所摧毁的旧制度。
en: Every account of Egypt’s agrarian history describes this system. But there was a second method for storing water, which was used to produce a second crop, in early summer, after the main winter harvest – and even a third crop, in the autumn.
The improvements introduced under Muhammad Ali were designed in part to enhance this arrangement.

The water was stored not in the field basins but in a substrate beneath them. Convinced by the colonial irrigation engineers that the old system allowed only one main crop a year, ‘the land lying fallow during the rest of the year for want of irrigation water’, modern historians have never described the old system that later-nineteenth-century irrigation schemes destroyed.

zh: 尼罗河洪泛平原的土壤由两层组成，如
剖面所示：上层是冲积砂土和黏土，其相对不透水的物质构成围堤田区的底部，储存并缓慢吸收部分洪水；下层是砾石和砂的基质。这种更粗糙、颗粒状的物质可以蓄存大量
水分，水被截留在上覆黏土层之下。当洪水通过堤坝和运河的开口淹没田地表层时，也补给了下方的砾石层，水向下渗过黏土，或在河流上涨时从河床两侧直接渗入，或通过淹没田间挖的灌溉坑而进入。
即使在今天，尽管上游地表水库造成地下水减少、下游因此发生海水入侵（全球海平面上升又加剧了这一点），这种地下储存仍是世界上最大的地下水储层之一。
en: The soils of the Nile floodplain consist of two layers, as shown in crosssection in

: an upper level of alluvial sands and clays, whose relatively impermeable material forms the basins that stored and slowly absorbed some of the flood waters; and a substrate of gravel and sand. This more coarse and granular material could hold large amounts of

water trapped beneath the clayey soils above. As the flood waters inundated the surface of the fields via openings in the dykes and canals, they also recharged the gravel layer below, seeping down through the clays, or percolating directly from the sides of the riverbed as the river rose, or via the flooding of irrigation pits dug in the fields.

Even today, despite depletion by surface reservoirs upstream and consequent seawater intrusion downstream (exacerbated by rising global sea levels), this underground storage forms one of the largest groundwater reservoirs in the world.

zh: 第二季作物用水来自这个地下储层，使用的是置于大型砖砌水井之上的
，即畜力水车。
每一位埃及历史读者都熟悉
，但通常假定它是从尼罗河或运河中提水。然而，在二十世纪之前，耕作者主要用它从井中提水。它由一个由牛驱动的水平轮组成，带动两个由轴连接的竖直轮（见
）。较大的竖直轮通过一长串水罐从井中提水。安置
的那口井则不那么为人熟悉。它是一个大型腔体，通过挖一个直径约十米、深三米到十或十五米的坑建成，
深度取决于地下水位。坑壁用黏土砖砌成圆形墙体，砖在工地制作并烧制，以获得强度和抗水性（见
）。正如一份中世纪文献所述，为下沉这口井，地面的砌砖工在由金合欢木制成的环形木基上砌筑一层层砖石，其他人则用桶从坑底挖出淤泥和水，在框架下方挖掘。
en: The second crop was irrigated from this subterranean reservoir, using
, or animal-driven waterwheels, placed over large, brick-built wells.
The

is familiar to every reader of Egyptian history, but is usually assumed to have lifted water from the Nile or from a canal. Before the twentieth century, however, cultivators used it to raise water mainly from wells. It consisted of a horizontal wheel driven by an ox, turning two vertical wheels connected by an axle (see
). The larger of the vertical wheels lifted the water from the well in a chain of pots. The well over which the
was placed is less familiar. It was a large chamber, constructed by excavating a pit about ten metres in diameter, to a depth ranging from three metres to ten or fifteen metres,
depending on the level of the ground water. The sides were lined with a circular wall of clay bricks, produced on site and fired to impart strength and resistance to water (see

). To sink the well, as a medieval text relates, bricklayers at the surface laid courses of masonry on a ringshaped wooden base made of acacia, while other men used buckets to excavate silt and water from the bottom of the pit, digging beneath the frame.

zh: “随着它下面的土壤松动，”文献解释说，“又随着它自身的重量加上砌在其上的砖层而增加，它便沉入地下。”
当井达到所需深度后，砖块向内砌成拱形，形成一个支撑上方机械的拱顶，屋顶中央留出一个矩形开口，让
的竖直轮及其水桶链能够降入其中。
这些砖砌水井是景观中的永久特征，尽管除了地表的开口外，大部分都看不见。水车通常每年秋天在洪水到来前拆开，到下一个季节再重新组装。
en: ‘As the soil under it loosens’, the text explains, ‘and as its own weight increases with the brick courses laid upon it, it goes down into the ground.’

When the well reached its required depth, the bricks were arched inwards to form a vault to support the machinery above, leaving a rectangular slot at the centre of the roof through which the vertical wheel of the
and its chain of buckets could descend.

The brick-built wells were a permanent feature of the landscape, although except for the slot on the surface largely invisible. The waterwheels were typically disassembled each autumn before the flood waters arrived, then reassembled the following season.

zh: 春夏两季，
日夜转动，木制齿轮呻吟、吱呀作响。对任何访客来说，这都是乡村的一种独特声音。1845 年 3 月，按照
穆罕默德·阿里帕夏的命令，埃及工程师约瑟夫·赫克基扬在一个村庄住了几夜，调查大麻种植。在“埃及村庄夜间最安静地段的噪音与不便”中——这些曾令他十分烦恼——他列出了“沉重水车的吱呀声”。
外国访客通常乘船沿河旅行，很少在村庄和田野停留。他们通过乡村的声音景观来领会乡村生活，常常把埃及乡村夏季特有的声音描述为水车哀怨的吱呀声。“沿着这里，也就是阿斯旺下游七八英里的地方，从船上望去看不到任何植被，除了一片片生长茂盛的棕榈树，”最受欢迎的游记之一记载道，“但远处一定有土壤，因为萨基亚水车总在吱呀作响。”
这种声音景观的大部分很快就消失了。
en: As the
rotated, day and night through spring and summer, its wooden gear wheels groaned and squeaked. For any visitor, this was a distinctive sound of the countryside. In March 1845, at the order of

Muhammad Ali Pasha, the Egyptian engineer Joseph Hekekyan spent several nights in a village, investigating hemp cultivation. Among ‘the noises and inconveniences of the quietest part of an Egyptian village night’, which had greatly annoyed him, he listed ‘the creaking of the heavy waterwheels’.

Foreign visitors usually travelled through the country by boat on the river, seldom spending time in the villages and fields. They apprehended rural life through its soundscape, often describing the characteristic noise of the Egyptian countryside in summer as the doleful squeaking of the waterwheel. ‘Along here, seven or eight miles below Assouan, there is no vegetation in sight from the boat, except strips of thrifty palm-trees,’ recorded one of the most popular accounts, ‘but there must be soil beyond, for the sakiyas are always creaking.’
Much of this soundscape was soon to disappear.

zh: 根据中世纪农业历书——例如重印在马格里齐《赫塔特》中的那一部——在科普特历第五个月图巴月（1 月 9 日至 2 月 7 日），主要作物成熟时，农民会修复围堤田块中央的水井，然后取出并组装水车。
水井可能有数米深，但在许多情况下，砾石层在洪泛平原边缘——沿河床以及外缘——升得更高。边缘处抬高的地下水位所产生的压力，形成了人工水头，把水推向井口。
马格里齐告诉我们，每口井可灌溉四到六英亩；如果土地就在附近，伊本·马马提的历书具体指出，可多达十英亩。
根据这些历书，井中储水在生长季节逐渐减少，到阿比布月第十五天（7 月 9 日）达到最低水位，届时上涨的尼罗河会开始补给它们。
水井和水车对中世纪农业如此重要，尤其是对大型庄园上种植甘蔗和其他夏季作物而言，以至于文献常常把这类庄园称为“水车”（
en: According to the medieval agrarian almanacs, such as the one reproduced in the

of Maqrizi, in the month of Tuba (9 January to 7 February), the fifth month of the Coptic calendar, as the main crops were maturing, farmers would restore the wells in the middle of the field basins, then bring out and assemble the waterwheels.

While the wells might be several metres deep, in many cases the gravel layer rose higher at the edges of the floodplain, both along the riverbed and at the outer margin. The pressure of the raised water table at the edges created an artificial head, forcing the supply up towards the top of the well.
Each well, Maqrizi tells us, could irrigate four to six acres; or up to ten acres, the almanac of Ibn Mammati specifies, if the land was close by.

The wells were gradually depleted during the growing season, reaching their lowest level on the fifteenth day of Abib (9 July), according to the almanacs, at which point the rising Nile would begin to replenish them.

The wells and waterwheels were so important to medieval agriculture, especially for producing sugar cane and other summer crops on large estates, that the sources often refer to such estates as ‘waterwheels’ (

zh: 二十世纪之交，当欧洲土地投机者发现这些水井时，他们以为压力必定来自深处的地下储层，于是成立了几家自流井公司，投资开发这种新资源。没有发现任何自流泉，这些公司都失败了。
灌溉工程师后来承认，水井被洪水补给“令我们惊讶”。
他们请来牛津培养的地质学家哈特利·特拉弗斯·费拉尔——斯科特船长首次南极探险的老队员——到埃及调查。他的报告记载，在上埃及卢克索以北约二十五英里的基夫特镇，“可以看到一股洪水
流入一个萨基亚井坑，却没有抬高其中的水位”。他指出，围堤田块中估计仍有 40,600 台
，并补充说，“如果每台在洪水期被淹没的萨基亚水车都发生这种情况，那么通过这种方式进入洪积层的水量必定非常巨大”。
en: When European land speculators discovered these wells around the turn of the twentieth century, they assumed the pressure must come from reservoirs deep below and set up several artesian water companies to invest in exploiting this new resource. No artesian springs were found and the companies failed.
The recharging of the wells by the flood ‘came as a surprise to us’, the irrigation engineers later acknowledged.

They brought to Egypt an Oxford-trained geologist, Hartley Travers Ferrar, a veteran of Captain Scott’s first Antarctic expedition, to investigate. His report recorded that at Qift, a town in Upper Egypt about twenty-five miles north of Luxor, ‘a stream of flood water was seen
flowing into a sakia-pit without raising the level of the water in it’. Noting that there were still an estimated 40,600
in field basins, he added that ‘if this takes place at every sakia which is submerged during flood time, the quantity of water which passes into the diluvial beds by this means must be very great’.

zh: 砾石层延伸到整个洪泛平原之下。然而在洪水较强的年份，这种地下储存还可以由另一种储备来补充：让水积聚在低洼地，包括洪泛平原外缘的土地，甚至周围沙漠中相邻的干谷。低洼、积水的土地排水最慢，因此被种上亚麻——一种偏好较湿土壤的贵重作物，加工成亚麻布后，正如我们将看到的，又提供了另一种储存选择。
或者，低地可以被挖深，形成池塘，储存来年春季和夏季的灌溉水。许多这样的
，即蓄水池，在十九世纪仍在使用。
事实上，在十九世纪灌溉工程之前，沿着尼罗河洪泛平原的大片地区，这类池塘沿沙漠边缘形成了第二条河道。它们由地下水和多余的洪水补给，并在主要蓄水田区排空时蓄满，这个地表网络补充了水井，成为储存水的来源。
（事实上，穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者修建的深层“夏季运河”，在某些方面是这一系统的延伸，因为它们不仅由上涨的尼罗河供水，也由地下水渗流供水。）
在中埃及，一条古老的运河——优素福运河，像大多数古老运河一样，由这些河流次级河道之一形成——让多余的洪水排入一个更大的洼地，即位于开罗以北约五十英里的法尤姆盆地。在古代和中世纪，法尤姆成为该国最富生产力的农业区之一，也是其亚麻工业的中心。管理这些泄洪通道的使用，进一步降低了下游洪水过量的风险。
en: The gravel beds extended beneath the entire area of the floodplain. However, in years of stronger floods, this underground storage could be supplemented with another reserve by allowing water to collect in low-lying ground, including land at the outer edges of the floodplain, or even adjacent wadis in the surrounding desert. Being the slowest to drain, low-lying, waterlogged lands were planted with flax, a valuable crop that prefers wetter soil and provides, when processed into linen, as we will see, another storage option.
Or the lowlands could be deepened by excavation to form pools that stored irrigation water for the following spring and summer. Numerous such
, or storage ponds, were still in use in the nineteenth century.

In fact, along great stretches of the Nile floodplain, prior to the irrigation works of the nineteenth century, such pools formed a second river channel along the desert edge. Fed from ground water and surplus flood water, and filling as the main catch basins were emptying, this surface network supplemented the wells as a source of stored water.

(In fact, the deep ‘summer canals’ built by Muhammad Ali and his successors were, in some ways, an extension of this system, for they filled not only from the rising Nile but from the seepage of groundwater.)

In Middle Egypt, an ancient canal, the Bahr Yusif – formed, like most older canals, from one of these secondary channels of the river – allowed surplus flood water to escape to a much larger depression, the Fayyum basin, lying about fifty miles north of Cairo. In the ancient and medieval periods, Fayyum became one of the country’s most productive agricultural regions and a centre of its linen industry. Managing the use of these escapes further reduced the risk of excess floods downstream.

zh: 水井灌溉的主要作物是
，即高粱。这种夏季作物的种植如此广泛，以至于在围堤蓄水农业被消除之前，高粱一直是埃及的主食。
高粱原产于非洲半干旱地区，是一种适应供水不足或不稳定问题的谷物，这正是苏丹地带——尼罗河、尼日尔河和塞内加尔河——大型河流流域数千年来所实行的洪水退去后耕作制的典型特征。
与小麦等谷类相比，它的根要深得多，叶片能够在干旱期间暂停光合作用，
进入一种类似休眠的状态。
高粱还能耐受积水土壤和洪水，部分原因是它具有中等耐盐性，能够承受过饱和土壤中较高的盐度。
它是一种多用途作物，叶片和茎秆可为牲畜提供饲料，为面包烤炉提供燃料，为住房提供茅草。在洪水小的年份，如果冬季收成不好，农民会利用额外的井灌扩大高粱的夏季种植。为了进一步弥补冬季收成不佳，在第三个生长季，即秋季，种植高粱的面积会“大幅增加”，使小农“能够重新装满谷仓”。
穆罕默德·阿里治下对围堤蓄水系统的改良，促进了第三季高粱的种植。
因此，高粱既适应使用地下储水的挑战，也适应供水的变化。与此同时，它又是一种能够弥补这种变化所可能导致之短缺的资源。
en: The principal crop produced from the well irrigation was
, or sorghum. The cultivation of this summer-season crop was so extensive that sorghum served as the staple food of Egypt prior to the elimination of flood-basin agriculture.

Native to the semi-arid regions of Africa, sorghum is a grain adapted to the problems of light or variable water supply, typical of the flood-recession farming practised for millennia in the large river basins of the Sudanic belt – the Nile, Niger, and Senegal rivers.
Compared with cereals like wheat, it has much deeper roots, and its leaves are able to suspend photosynthesis during drought,
entering a kind of hibernation.
Sorghum also tolerates waterlogged soils and flooding, in part because it is moderately salt-tolerant, withstanding the higher salinity of over-saturated soils.

It is a multipurpose crop, its leaves and stalk supplying forage for livestock, fuel for bread ovens, and thatch for housing. In years of low floods, if the winter harvest was poor, farmers expanded the summer cultivation of sorghum using additional well irrigation. To further compensate for a poor winter harvest, in the third growing season, the autumn, the area planted with sorghum would be ‘very considerably increased’, enabling small farmers ‘to refill their granaries’.
The improvements to the basin system under Muhammad Ali facilitated this cultivation of sorghum in the third season.

Thus sorghum was suited to the challenges of using stored subterranean water and to variations in water supply. At the same time, it was a resource that could remedy the shortages to which such variability might lead.

zh: 水井还被用来种植小块果园水果和其他有价值的夏季作物，包括靛蓝作物、芝麻、棉花和甘蔗，以及种植富含养分的芋头（
）。这是一种根茎类作物，在湿润土壤中生长旺盛，实际上浸在水中长得更好，因此可以留在地里一直到秋季下一季洪水开始上涨之时。芋头被该国奥斯曼—土耳其精英视为美味，每英亩收入是棉花或甘蔗的两倍，生长时间却只有一半。一份资料告诉我们，一个土地很少的大家庭可能靠一英亩芋头生活。
en: The wells were also used to cultivate smaller areas of orchard fruits and other valuable summer crops, including indigo, sesame, cotton, and sugar cane, and to grow the nutrient-rich Colocasia (

), or taro, a root crop that flourishes in moist soil and in fact grows better when submerged in water, allowing it to remain in the ground even into autumn when the next season’s flood began to rise. Prized as a delicacy by the country’s Ottoman-Turkish elite, taro produced twice the income per acre of cotton or sugar cane in half the growing time. A large household with little land, one source tells us, might live off an acre of taro.

zh: 公共储存
en: Public Storage

zh: 与英国人要用来取代它的河流拦河堰、永久地表水库和所谓常年灌溉系统相比，在地表之下储水有几个优势。第一，旧系统让田地得以被淹没，并沉积富含养分的淤泥。土壤既因淤泥中的硝酸盐、磷酸盐和微量金属而肥沃，也因淹没期间土地被迫休养而肥沃。新的拦河堰和水库将摧毁这一自行运转的泛滥与增肥过程，使全年从运河提水和机械施肥都需要繁重劳动和高昂费用。每一部历史叙述都顺带提到新系统的这一后果和旧系统的优势。更多的好处则很少被提及。
en: Storing water beneath the surface had several advantages compared to the system of river barrages, permanent surface reservoirs, and so-called perennial irrigation with which the British were to replace it. First, the old system allowed the inundation of the fields and depositing of nutrient-rich sediment. Soils were enriched both by the nitrates, phosphates, and trace metals in the sediment and by the enforced resting of the land during inundation. The new barrages and reservoirs were to destroy this self-moving process of flooding and fertilisation, creating a need for the heavy labour and expense of year-round water lifting from canals and mechanical fertilisation. Every historical account notes in passing this consequence of the new system and the advantage of the old. The further benefits are seldom noted.

zh: 第二个优势是，这种自然发生的肥力补充在两个方向上横向流动：先是洪水，然后是退水。河流每年的扩张和收缩，使营养物质和生物在河道与洪泛平原之间双向交换，维持着陆地、鸟类和水生生命。
摧毁季节性的“洪水脉冲”——水文学家现在这样称呼它——消除了维系陆地与水中生命繁衍的相互作用，包括鸟类和水禽，以及大量鱼类及其食物来源，它们的筑巢、产卵和迁徙周期依赖于洪水周期及其提供的养分。
洪水退去时，把网放在把水送回河流的渠道口，就能获得丰收。
人们还在田里用手捉鱼，使用芦苇陷阱，或从水排入的水井中捕鱼——这使地下蓄水池发挥了第二种作用，即鱼塘。
据报道，可放在陶罐中储存数月之久的腌鱼，是普通人最常食用的动物性食物。
幼鱼还捕食蚊幼虫，防止疟疾传播，而疟疾在更南方的尼罗河流域国家为地方性流行病。
en: The second advantage was that this self-moving enrichment flowed laterally in both directions, first the flood and then the ebb. The annual expansion and contraction of the stream allowed the two-way exchange of nutrients and biota between the river channel and the floodplain, sustaining terrestrial, avian, and aquatic life.

Destroying the seasonal ‘flood pulse’, as hydrologists now call it, eliminated interactions that reproduced life on both land and water, including birds and waterfowl and an abundance of fish and their food sources, whose cycles of nesting, spawning, and migration depended on the flood cycle and the nutrients it supplied.
When the flood receded, fishing nets placed at the mouth of the channels that carried the waters back to the river yielded an abundant catch.
Fish were also caught by hand in the fields, using reed traps, or from the wells into which the waters drained – allowing the underground cisterns to serve a second role, as fish tanks.
Cured fish, which could be stored in earthenware pots for months, was reportedly the animal food that ordinary people consumed most often.
Young fish also preyed on mosquito larvae, preventing the spread of malaria, which was endemic in Nile Basin countries farther south.

zh: 第三，采用底土储水时，储存的水很少因蒸发而损失。在常年灌溉下，大量水从新水库和扩大的河流表面积蒸发。与此同时，每年淹没田地，然后把洪水储存在地表之下，再随着河流回到最低水位而缓慢释放回河道，会自然地排干土地，把有害盐分冲洗到根区以下。河流的涨落还冲洗并晾干了往返田间的支渠，清除了杂草和害虫。使用拦河堰和大坝的常年灌溉把平均河流水位和地下水位抬高了几米，导致土壤积水和日益盐碱化、作物产量下降，并需要大量排水沟和泵。支渠变成了静止的永久沟渠，成了水葫芦的人造避风港——这种浮水植物由欧洲人作为观赏植物引入——它那为抵抗亚马逊河急流而演化出的纤维根垫，开始堵塞下埃及的水道和湖泊（在殖民地印度、美国南部以及后来整个尼罗河流域的主要河流中也是如此），使蒸发造成的水损失翻倍，并杀死其他生命形式。
en: Third, with subsoil storage, little of the stored water was lost by evaporation. Under perennial irrigation, large volumes of water evaporated from the new reservoirs and from the expanded surface area of the river. At the same time, inundating the fields each year, then storing the flood waters below the surface, from where they were slowly released back into the river channel as it returned to its minimum level, automatically drained the land and flushed harmful salts to below the root zone. The flood and ebb of the river also flushed and dried the branch canals that carried waters to and from the fields, cleaning them of weeds and pests. Perennial irrigation using barrages and dams raised the average river level and water table by several metres, leading to waterlogged and increasingly saline soils, declining crop yields, and the need for extensive drains and pumps. Transformed into still, permanent ditches, the branch canals became a manufactured haven for water hyacinth – the floating plant introduced as an ornamental by Europeans – whose fibrous root mats, developed to resist the fast-flowing rivers of Amazonia, began to clog the waterways and lakes of Lower Egypt (as it did the major rivers of colonial India, the southern United States, and later the entire Nile Basin), doubling the loss of water by evaporation and killing off other forms of life.

zh: 第四，永久运河及其河岸也成为携带埃及血吸虫病和钩虫病的螺类和线虫的滋生地。正如珍妮弗·德尔所解释的，这两种
使人衰弱的寄生虫感染成为埃及乡村的地方病，缓慢地殖民了相当一部分人口的身体。
在新灌溉制度下，这些身体还因日益严重的营养不良而衰弱，特别是糙皮病的传播。运河系统促进了棉花的广泛种植，这又鼓励人们改吃玉米（美洲玉米）；玉米夏季生长期短，与棉花的两年轮作相吻合，其秸秆还可在从南威尔士进口煤炭之外充当燃料，用于蒸汽灌溉泵的锅炉。
大量工人从上埃及种植高粱的地区转移到下三角洲劳动密集的棉花种植园，促成了饮食的这一变化。与其他谷物不同，玉米不提供烟酸（维生素 B3），除非在碱性溶液中煮沸，这正是其原产地墨西哥制作玉米饼粉的方法。糙皮病由缺乏烟酸引起，会造成皮肤和消化系统的疼痛性损伤，以及痴呆，有时甚至死亡。英国人对痴呆率上升感到惊恐。
洪水的消除以及棉花和甘蔗种植的指数级增长，还使其他感染、寄生虫和害虫得以大量繁殖。
老鼠被甘蔗汁吸引，而甘蔗高大的茎秆保护它们免受猛禽捕食，于是大量侵扰甘蔗田。它们啃咬甘蔗基部，可毁掉多达四分之一的收成。
最具破坏性的害虫是棉叶虫——一种蛾（
），其幼虫因棉花种植扩大而大量繁殖。如果不逐片摘除受虫害的叶子，它们能毁掉整片棉花田。
en: Fourth, the permanent canals and their banks also became breeding grounds for the snails and nematodes that carried bilharzia (schistosomiasis) and hookworm disease. As Jennifer Derr explains, these two
debilitating parasitic infections became endemic to rural Egypt, slowly colonising the bodies of a significant part of the population.

Those bodies were also weakened under the new irrigation regime by increasing malnutrition, in particular the spread of pellagra. The canal system facilitated the widespread cultivation of cotton, which encouraged a switch to the consumption of maize (American corn), whose short summer growing season synchronised with the two-year rotation of cotton, and whose straw supplemented imports of coal from south Wales as fuel for the boilers of the steam-driven irrigation pumps.

A great transfer of workers from the sorghum-growing regions of Upper Egypt to the labour-intensive cotton plantations of the lower Delta contributed to this change in diet. Unlike other grains, maize does not supply niacin (vitamin B3), unless boiled in an alkaline solution, the method used in making tortilla flour in its native Mexico. Caused by lack of niacin, pellagra results in painful damage to the skin and digestive system, and in dementia and sometimes death. The British became alarmed at increasing rates of dementia.
The elimination of the flood and the exponential increase in cotton and cane cultivation also allowed other infections, parasites, and pests to flourish.
Rats, attracted to the juice of sugar cane, whose tall stalks protect them from birds of prey, infested cane fields. By gnawing the base of the canes, they could destroy up to a quarter of the crop.
The most destructive pest was the cotton worm, a moth (
) whose larvae thrived on the increased cultivation of cotton. They could destroy entire fields of cotton if not checked by picking off the infected leaves one by one.

zh: 与水库和运河中的新储水方式相比，储存在土壤下的水还有一个优势。与地表水不同，它不受强大的种植园主——他们可能垄断新运河的使用权——以及为他们服务的灌溉工程师的控制。“在这里，我们看到围堤蓄水灌溉达到了最佳状态，”一份对索哈杰省的调查指出；这个南部地区尚未遭受邻省那种破坏性工程，尤其是更北边建立的大片甘蔗种植园。“土地肥沃，作物繁茂，人民富裕而独立，底土水得到充分利用。”这些农民享有显著的独立与繁荣：“没有任何工程师能够截断他们的洪水，而水位便于利用的充沛地下水则是他们自己的财产。”
en: Water stored beneath the soil had one further advantage over the new storage in reservoirs and canals. Unlike water held on the surface, it was beyond the control of powerful plantation owners, who might monopolise access to the new canals, and of the irrigation engineers who served their needs. ‘Here we see basin irrigation at its best’, noted a survey of the province of Sohaj, a region in the south that had not yet suffered the damaging engineering work of neighbouring provinces, in particular the extensive sugar plantations created further north. ‘The land is rich, the crops luxuriant, the people well off and independent, and the subsoil water well utilised.’ Farmers ‘whose flood waters no engineer can cut off, and whose plentiful subsoil water at a convenient level is their own property’, enjoyed a notable independence and prosperity.

zh: 水车本身是人、动物、土壤和作物之间复杂互动的焦点。它们通常由牛拉动，牛的饲料——主要是埃及三叶草——可以种在
同一片田里，一次种植可收割三次以上，还能改善土壤。牛会繁殖自己的后代，从而延续这个国家的主要动力来源。正如在大多数农业社会（包括欧洲的农业社会）中一样，饲养它们是储存和增加家庭财富的主要手段（英语中 cattle 一词源自 chattel 或 capital，意为“存货”；其含义到十六世纪才收窄为
用牛作为灌溉劳力，使公犊有了价值；后来用机械泵取代它们，使公犊在很大程度上变得无用，迫使它们被宰杀作肉食，并导致以肉为基础的饮食增加。牛粪被做成扁饼，在阳光下晒干，储存在屋顶上，用作烘焙和烹饪的燃料。
水井对国家的丝绸生产也变得重要。埃及以前依赖进口丝线，在十九世纪之交发展了自己的养蚕业。到 1820 年代，提供蚕蛾幼虫食物的桑树数量估计达到三百万棵。蚕蛾是一种家养昆虫（事实上是除蜜蜂之外唯一被家养的昆虫），它产下的卵需要凉爽处孵化，因此被储存在灌溉井中。
en: The waterwheels themselves were the focus of a complex interaction among humans, animals, soils, and crops. They were usually turned by oxen, whose fodder – mostly Egyptian clover – could be grown in the

same fields, supplying three or more cuttings from a single planting and improving the soil. Cattle produced their own young, thus reproducing the country’s main source of motive power. As in most agrarian societies, including those of Europe, rearing them was a principal means of storing and increasing household wealth (in English, the word cattle derives from chattel or capital, meaning stock; its sense narrowed to
stock only in the sixteenth century).

Using oxen as irrigation labour gave value to male calves; their replacement with mechanical pumps would later render the males largely useless, forcing their slaughter for meat and an increase in meat-based diets. Cattle dung, formed into flat cakes, dried in the sun, and stored on rooftops, provided fuel for baking and cooking.

The wells also became important to the country’s silk production. Previously reliant on imported thread, Egypt developed a domestic silkworm industry at the turn of the nineteenth century. By the 1820s, the number of mulberry trees, whose leaves provide the food for the larvae of the silk moth, reached an estimated three million. The silk moth, a domesticated insect (the only one, in fact, besides the honeybee), produces eggs that require a cool place to incubate; they were therefore stored in the irrigation wells.

zh: 建造一口井需要砖匠制作烧砖，也需要砌砖工施工。水井机械需要木匠制造水轮，并每季拆装，这维持了村庄中最大的非农业生计。
为了转动机械，最多有八头牛轮班工作，因此通常会有多户人家共用一台水轮，通过一个浅田沟网络把水分配给各个地块。
这种合作使水轮日夜转动，也包括挖掘和维护沟渠、种植供养人和动物的作物等劳动。
合作并不意味着和谐或没有强制；与任何共同体一样，家庭内部和家庭之间的等级关系会塑造任务的分配。
二十世纪的记述把这种合作安排的残存实例称为“
合作圈”。农民往往通过亲属关系联系在一起，每人提供自己的役畜，有时参加不止一个合作圈。
在苏丹北部和努比亚，上涨的尼罗河通常留在河道内，很少淹没更广阔的洪泛平原，因此使用
如此普遍，以至于这个词被用来指村庄本身，即围绕水车合作形成的共同体。
在上埃及，主要的夏收节不是在收割高粱时庆祝，而是在
完成对作物的第十次、也是最后一次灌溉时庆祝。人们把
或其他甜食带到田里的水车旁分享，然后把吃空的盘子装满高粱穗送回；主人会再割下四穗，系在转动水轮的两头牛额头上，然后心怀感激与喜悦地把它们赶回家。
en: Building a well required brickmakers to make fired bricks and bricklayers to construct it. The well machinery needed carpenters to fabricate the wheel and assemble and disassemble it each season, sustaining the largest non-farming livelihood in the villages.

To turn the machine, up to eight oxen worked in shifts, so a number of houses would typically share in each wheel, which distributed the water to individual plots via a network of shallow field ditches.
The collaboration kept the wheel turning day and night, and included the labour of those who dug and maintained the ditches and grew the crops that fed humans and animals alike.
Collaboration does not imply harmony or the absence of compulsion; as in any community, hierarchies within and among households would shape the allocation of tasks.
Twentieth-century accounts describe surviving instances of this cooperative arrangement as a ‘
ring’. Often linked by kinship, the farmers each provided their own draft animal, sometimes participating in more than one ring.
In northern Sudan and Nubia, where the rising Nile usually remained within its channel and seldom inundated the wider floodplain, using the
was so universal that the word came to refer to the village itself, a community formed through the collaboration around the wheel.
In Upper Egypt, the main summer harvest feast was celebrated not when the sorghum was cut but when the
completed the tenth and final watering of the crop. After sharing

or other sweetmeats brought out to the waterwheel in the field, then returning the empty plates piled with heads of sorghum, the owner would cut four more heads and fasten them to the foreheads of the two oxen that had turned the wheel, before driving them home in gratitude and celebration.

zh: 在那些由包税人或其他收入权利持有者索取一部分收成的土地上——这种安排在个人土地所有权于十九世纪后期重新出现之前，广泛用于马穆鲁克和奥斯曼时期——围绕水车的合作会包括所谓的“协助”（
），即强制性劳动，为主张这些权利的人经营水井。
在前现代时期，萨基亚水车系统的周期性扩张可能与甘蔗种植园的发展有关，这些种植园需要在更大规模上使用人力和畜力的强制劳动。
从 1820 年代起，随着开罗政权开始重新殖民该国南部，发给负责建立大型农业庄园的官员的首批命令就是取得牛只并“架设水车”。
到该世纪后期，尤其在 1863—4 年大牛瘟之后，统治家族和其他大庄园主开始用英国制造的蒸汽泵取代
；这些泵最初太重，无法在年度泛滥前拆卸移走，但又足够坚固，能在“每次洪水时被完全淹没”后幸存。
工程师随后改装了
——一种蒸汽动力犁——作为移动泵，在洪水退去后可以推到田间架在水井上。
与此同时，大多数农民继续依赖
，不过在二十世纪，他们逐渐先用柴油泵、后用小型电动泵取代了它（如今可以用太阳能供电）。

然而，这些提水装置的使用越来越局限于从新灌溉运河中提水。水如今被远程储存在上游拦河堰和大坝之后，尤其是在阿斯旺大坝于 1912 年和 1933 年两次加高、1937 年在喀土穆上游白尼罗河的杰贝勒奥利亚修建第二座大坝之后；1960 年代建成规模大得多的阿斯旺高坝，以及 2020 年埃塞俄比亚在青尼罗河上建成第二座巨型拦河坝——埃塞俄比亚复兴大坝之后，这种情况更加明显。随着尼罗河洪水及其益处被消除，灌溉水如今可以全年从运河抽水获得，地下蓄水系统在很大程度上被废弃了。
en: On lands where a share of the produce was claimed by a tax farmer or other holder of rights to revenue, an arrangement widely used in the Mamluk and Ottoman periods, prior to the re-emergence of individual proprietorship in the late nineteenth century, the collaboration around the waterwheel would include the ‘assistance’ (
), meaning obligatory labour, required to run the wells of the person claiming those rights.
The periodic expansion of the
system in pre-modern times may have been associated with the development of sugar plantations, requiring compulsory labour, both human and animal, on a larger scale.
From the 1820s, as the regime in Cairo began to recolonise the south of the country, the first orders to officials creating large agricultural estates were to secure cattle and ‘erect waterwheels’.
Later in the century, especially after the great cattle plague of 1863–4, the ruling household and other owners of large estates began to replace

with British-built steam pumps, which initially were too heavy to disassemble and remove before the annual inundation but were robust enough to survive being ‘completely buried under water every flood’.
Engineers then adapted the locomobile, a steam-powered plough, to serve as a mobile pump that could be wheeled into the fields and placed over wells when the flood receded.
Meanwhile, most farmers continued to rely on
, although, in the twentieth century, they gradually replaced them first with diesel pumps and later with small electric pumps (which today can be solar-powered).

However, their use was increasingly restricted to lifting water from the new irrigation canals. The water was now stored remotely, behind barrages and large dams upstream, especially after the height of the Aswan Dam was raised, in 1912 and again in 1933, and a second dam was built in 1937, at Gebel Aulia, on the White Nile just above Khartoum, and more so after the completion of a much larger structure, the Aswan High Dam, in the 1960s, and of a second giant barrage, the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia, in 2020. With the elimination of the Nile flood and its benefits and with irrigation water now available by pumping it year-round from canals, the subterranean storage system was largely abandoned.

zh: 让萨基亚水车沉默
en: Silencing the Saqiya

zh: 水车和水井已经消失。它们既从河流的使用方式中被消除，也从埃及殖民过程的描述中被消除。它们从河流历史中消失，可以为我们提供线索，说明它们为何从景观中被移除。随着它们一起从视野中消失的，是河流本身的生态、储存的经济，以及它们所促成的生活方式。这促使我们提出刚刚那个问题：水车会吱呀作响吗？如果我们永远无法充分还原殖民主义所沉默的庶民声音，那么还有其他沉默、其他声音和其他能动性——人类的与非人类的——同样难以恢复，但关于攫取装置的叙述仍然可以尝试承认它们。
en: The waterwheel and the well have disappeared. They have been eliminated both from the way the river is used and the way the colonising of Egypt is described. Their elimination from the history of the river can offer us clues as to why they were removed from the landscape. With them have vanished from sight the very ecology of the river and the economy of storage and modes of life they enabled. This motivates the question we have just posed: Can the waterwheel squeak? If we can never adequately recapture the subaltern voices that colonialism silences, there are other silences, other sounds, and other agencies, human and nonhuman, that are equally difficult to recover, but that an account of apparatuses of capture can nevertheless try to acknowledge.

zh: 消失有三个原因。每一个原因都告诉我们一些关于剩余如何被攫取、以及这种攫取如何被重组的情况。第一，关于欧洲殖民之前尼罗河历史的最佳叙述，大多基于关注某种特定河流治理方式的资料。它们的焦点是实施权威和抽取收入的大型工程。
一个主要来源是一份名为
（苏丹堤堰登记册）的政府登记簿。奥斯曼人在十六世纪征服埃及后编纂了这份登记簿，它以更早的记录为基础，是一部描述管理河流流量的地表渠道的汇编。
一词指堤岸或土堤，其维护确保洪水被妥善控制，既包括河岸，也包括把河水送往围堤田块和泄洪道的运河。这些登记簿在十九世纪后期仍然可用，当时它们似乎是该国灌溉网络最全面记述的来源，即阿里帕夏·穆巴拉克的《赫塔特》。穆巴拉克是一位主要工程师和公职人员，他把该著作的第 18、19 卷用于逐村描述灌溉基础设施。
en: There are three reasons for the disappearance of the

. Each tells us something about the way surplus was captured and how its capturing was to be reorganised. First, the best accounts of the history of the Nile prior to European colonisation are based largely upon sources that were concerned with a specific mode of governing the river. Their focus is the large-scale works through which authority was exercised and revenue extracted.
A principal source is a government register known as

. Compiled by the Ottomans after they conquered Egypt in the sixteenth century, and based on older records, the register is a compendium describing the channels on the surface through which the flow of the river was managed.
The term

refers to the embankments or dykes whose upkeep ensured that the flood waters were properly contained, encompassing both the banks of the river and the canals that carried its water to field basins and escapes. The registers were still available in the late nineteenth century, when they appear to have been a source for the most comprehensive account of the country’s irrigation network, Ali Pasha Mubarak’s
. A leading engineer and public official, Mubarak devoted volumes 18 and 19 of that work to describing village by village the infrastructure of irrigation.

zh: 直接或间接利用这些登记簿来描述灌溉系统的著作，只是偶尔提到水井和操作水井的
。人们可以为此提出一个直接的理由。作为大型基础设施，运河和堤岸要求并促成了更广泛的权威结构的发展，这反映在登记簿的维护上。而水车和水井是分散的本地设备，并未产生这种效果。水车是一种临时装置，
每季组装和拆卸，由家庭拥有和维护，不为建立政府的权力或主张提供基础设施。因此，它们没有被“登记”。
en: Writings that draw on these registers, directly or indirectly, to describe the irrigation system make only occasional mention of wells and the

that worked them. One could suggest a straightforward reason for this. As large-scale infrastructures, the canals and embankments required and enabled the development of a wider structure of authority, reflected in the maintaining of registers. As discrete, local equipment, the waterwheels and wells did not. A temporary apparatus

assembled and disassembled each season, owned and maintained by households, the waterwheel provided no infrastructure for building the powers or claims of government. They were not, therefore, ‘registered’.

zh: 技术装置与权威行使之间的同样关系，也见于尼罗河历史的第二个主要来源——法律制度的记录。法庭处理的案件中，陌生人之间的纠纷占了不成比例的高份额；它们或许更关注同样的大型基础设施所产生的问题。运河以水车所没有的方式制造冲突，因为它们穿越多处地产和社区，容易受到阻断和争议。驱动水轮的牛可能在陌生人之间交易，或挣脱束缚损坏他人财产，因此，如果
出现在文献中，往往与动物纠纷有关。
法律制度围绕这些问题扩展，而这些问题正是书写河流历史的主要题材。
en: The same relation between a technical apparatus and the exercise of authority is seen in a second major source for histories of the Nile, the records of the legal system. Court cases dealt disproportionately with disputes among strangers; they were perhaps more concerned with the problems produced by the same large-scale infrastructure. Canals created conflict in ways that waterwheels did not, for they traversed multiple properties and communities and were easily subject to interruption and dispute. The oxen that drove the wheels might be traded among strangers, or break loose and damage another property, so, if the
appears in the sources, it is often in relation to disputes over animals.
The legal system expanded around such issues, and these were the main topics around which the history of the river could be written.

zh: 相比之下，反映社区内部纠纷解决的资料，例如地方法学家（
，穆夫提）用来不诉诸法院而解决冲突的法律手册，可以更多地揭示
的社会世界。“如果一个人借用他人的牛来配自己的
使用，而牛掉进井里，”一部最广泛使用的手册解释说，“那么他应承担责任。”
用运河和水库系统取代
，与地方法学意见被法院系统和政府登记簿体系取代是同步发生的；扩展的基础设施促成并依赖后者。换言之，水轮在历史资料中的出现或缺失，可能不仅反映不同的灌溉手段，也反映正义与权力形式的扩张或消退。
en: By contrast, sources that reflect the resolution of disputes within the community, such as the legal manuals used by local jurists (
) to settle conflicts without resort to the court system, can reveal more about the social world of the
. ‘If a person borrows another’s ox to use with his
and it falls into the well’, one of the most widely used manuals explains, ‘then he is liable for it’.
The replacement of the

by a system of canals and reservoirs went hand in hand with the displacement of local juridical opinion by the system of courts and government registers that an expanded infrastructure enabled and depended upon. In other words, the presence or absence of the water-wheel in historical sources may reflect not just alternative means of irrigation but expanding or receding forms of justice and power.

zh: 的消失，还因为许多现代论述依赖欧洲资料，尤其是那些在穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者治下帮助发展尼罗河灌溉工程的法国工程师。工程师的关注点——被后来历史学家复制——是那些工程。许多当代学者依赖罗杰·欧文的经典叙述，而欧文依赖让·马聚埃尔 1937 年的著作，马聚埃尔又借鉴利南·德·贝勒丰 1874 年的研究，据此提出下埃及只有大约八分之一的农田用于种植夏季作物，上埃及更少。这个数字是那个错误观念的主要来源：全国大部分土地每年只生产一季作物。但利南只提到由新夏季运河供水的面积。他指出，有权势的地主垄断了运河，而普通农民，
“那些挖了运河的人，却不得不用井水供应夏季种植园，靠萨基亚水车提水”。他表示，
灌溉的面积要大得多——但没有记录在夏季种植面积的估算中。
en: The disappearance of the

was further caused by the reliance of many modern accounts on European sources, especially the French engineers who helped develop Nile irrigation works under Muhammad Ali and his successors. The focus of the engineers, reproduced by more recent historians, was those schemes. Many contemporary scholars depend on the classic account by Roger Owen, who relies on Jean Mazuel’s work of 1937, who drew on Linant de Bellefonds’s 1874 study, to suggest that only about an eighth of the agricultural land in Lower Egypt was used to grow summer crops, and even less in Upper Egypt. This figure was a principal source for the erroneous idea that most of the country’s land produced only a single crop each year. But Linant was referring only to the area fed by the new summer canals. He noted that powerful proprietors monopolised the canals, while ordinary farmers,
‘who have dug the canals, are obliged to supply their summer plantations with water from wells, raised by means of sakiehs’. The
, he indicated, irrigated a far larger area – but were not recorded in the estimates of land devoted to summer cultivation.
