zh: 然而，水井灌溉系统消失的主要原因是英国人努力消除它，既从河流的管理方式中，也从其历史的书写方式中消除。英国占领后被迫靠边的埃及工程师了解大型夏季运河的有害影响，尤其是 1870 年代为该国统治者赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔的甘蔗种植园而建的易卜拉希米亚运河；他们主张保留围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉系统。工程师阿里·穆巴拉克在赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔最后一届政府中担任公共工程大臣（1878—9），就在英国和法国施压奥斯曼苏丹解除赫迪夫职务之前。1879 年，穆巴拉克在离任期间出版了一本关于尼罗河管理的书，

children: Nukhbat al-fikr fi tadbir nil Misr

zh: （《尼罗河治理精要》），提出了一系列建议，以改善现有的混合种植制度和以河谷为基础（而非完全以河流为基础）的蓄水：延长水在围堤田块中的储存时间，并更缓慢地排放；在侧谷和洼地建设额外储水；增加小型拦河堰，以提高三角洲部分地区的河流水位。他反对扩大棉花和甘蔗种植，部分原因是种植这些作物在犁地、播种、田间管理和收获，以及挖掘和清理夏季灌溉运河方面需要大量强制劳动。他编制数字表格，表明埃及在 1800 年围堤蓄水农业下种植的粮食和纤维作物组合，比 1860 年代广泛种植的棉花和甘蔗更有价值。他还主张，更丰富的作物多样性支持畜牧业，以及一系列以羊毛、亚麻和其他纤维加工为基础的本地工业。
en: The main reason for the disappearance of the system of well irrigation, however, is that the British worked to eliminate it, both from how the river was managed and how its history was written. Egyptian engineers, forced aside after the British occupation, and aware of the deleterious effects of the large summer canals, especially the Ibrahimiya Canal built in the 1870s to serve the sugar plantations of Khedive Isma‘il, the country’s ruler, had argued in favour of retaining the system of catch basins and well irrigation. The engineer Ali Mubarak served as Minister of Public Works in Khedive Isma‘il’s final government in 1878–9, just before Britain and France pressured the Ottoman sultan to remove the Khedive from power. In 1879, while out of office, Mubarak published a book on the management of the Nile,

children: Nukhbat al-fikr fi tadbir nil Misr

en: , which made a series of proposals for improving the existing mixed-crop system and valley-based (rather than exclusively river-based) water storage: increasing the length of time water was stored in field basins, and releasing it more slowly; building additional storage in side valleys and depressions; and adding small barrages to raise the level of the river in parts of the Delta. He opposed the increased cultivation of cotton and sugar cane, in part because of the quantity of forced labour they required for ploughing, planting, tending, and harvesting and for digging and clearing the summer irrigation canals. He produced tables of figures to demonstrate that the mix of food and fibre crops Egypt cultivated under flood-basin farming in 1800 was more valuable than the extensively grown cotton and cane of the 1860s. He also argued that the greater diversity of crops supported animal husbandry and a range of local industries based on the processing of wool, flax, and other fibres.

zh: 英国官员不得不努力贬低这些观点，尤其因为这些观点起初得到最有见识的殖民灌溉专家威廉·威尔科克斯本人的支持。威尔科克斯后来成为埃及政府的蓄水系统主管和第一座阿斯旺大坝的设计者，也是《埃及灌溉》的作者；这部综合性研究在 1913 年出版、长达 900 页的第三版，是后来这一领域每一位历史学家所依赖的。然而，在该报告 1889 年出版、仅 350 页的第一版中，即英国
占领仅七年之后，威尔科克斯主张保留甚至重新扩大围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉系统。他收集的数据表明，围堤蓄水系统比把土地改为运河灌溉更具生产力和利润，部分原因是“在围堤田区中种植一英亩作物的成本微不足道”。
虽然三角洲拦河堰的完工使低洼土地能够通过永久运河灌溉，但即使在下埃及，“在 8 米等高线以上（海拔），水井被大量用于灌溉”，而在上埃及的围堤田区中，“到处都挖井进行夏季灌溉”，从而实现第二、第三个生长季。
英国占领后出版的其他记述也提出了类似论点。
与阿里·穆巴拉克一样，威尔科克斯和其他工程师更倾向于把多余的洪水储存在河谷一侧的泄水区，而不是在河流本身筑坝，并希望有一天，当人们对新运河系统和拦河堰的后果“感到绝望”时，三角洲能恢复整个南部仍在使用的泛滥过程，重新引入“旧的健康制度：土地每年由尼罗河本身冲洗、熟化和施钙，无需任何其他媒介”。
en: British officials had to work hard to discredit these views, especially when they were supported at first by the most knowledgeable of the colonial irrigation experts, William Willcocks himself. The man who would become director of reservoirs in the Egyptian government and the architect of the first Aswan Dam, Willcocks was the author of

, a compendious study on whose third edition, published in 1913 and 900 pages long, every later historian in this area relies. In the first edition of that report, however, only 350 pages in length and published in 1889, just seven years after the British

occupation, Willcocks argued for retaining and even re-expanding the system of catch basins and irrigation from wells. He compiled figures showing that the flood-basin system was more productive and profitable than converting land to canal irrigation, in part because ‘the cost of raising crops on an acre of land in the basins is insignificant’.

While completing the Delta Barrage had allowed the irrigation of lower-lying lands by permanent canals, it was still the case even in Lower Egypt that ‘above an 8-meter contour [above sea level], wells are freely used for irrigation’, while in the basins of Upper Egypt ‘wells are dug everywhere for summer irrigation’, allowing a second and third growing season.
Other accounts published after the British occupation made similar arguments.

Like Ali Mubarak, Willcocks and other engineers preferred schemes for storing surplus flood waters in escapes at the side of the valley, rather than the damming of the river itself, and hoped that one day, when people were ‘in despair’ at the consequences of the new canal system and barrages, the Delta would be restored to the process of inundation still used throughout the south, reintroducing ‘the old healthy system, by which the land is washed, matured, and limed annually by the Nile itself without any other agency’.

zh: 在伦敦和纽约两地出版，部分面向“有意投资土地开垦计划的人”。
然而，威尔科克斯的上司贾斯廷·罗斯中校在第一版中加上了自己的导言，说作者支持围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉的论点是错误的。罗斯是英国带到埃及的八名在印度受训的灌溉工程师之一（威尔科克斯也在其中），不久前被提升为灌溉总监，地位超过威尔科克斯。他上任后的最初行动之一，就是改写威尔科克斯的计算，声称水井灌溉只允许在 10% 的土地上种植夏季高粱。其余 90% 在夏季将闲置，“因为劳动力稀缺”。
这一计算使旧制度显得生产力较低。且不说蒸汽泵可以取代人力和畜力在围堤蓄水田区提井水——这一发展已在进行中——劳动力稀缺有两个原因，其中之一我们将在下文讨论。
但正如威尔科克斯本人所解释的，直接原因是南部村庄的男丁被抽空，为北方提供劳动力，去挖掘和维护棉花种植如今所依赖的运河系统；他们要么被强制劳动驱使，要么按合同受雇，工资由公共资金支付。
换言之，
使北方新运河系统如此昂贵的非凡劳动力需求，被反常地用来使
系统显得不切实际。
en: was published in New York as well as London, intended in part for ‘persons desirous of investing money in land reclamation schemes’.

However, Willcocks’s superior, Lieutenant Colonel Justin Ross, added his own introduction to the first edition, saying that the author’s argument in favour of flood basins and well irrigation was wrong. One of eight Indian-trained irrigation engineers, including Willcocks, whom the British had brought to Egypt, Ross had recently been promoted over him as inspector general of irrigation. In one of his first acts on becoming his supervisor, he reworked Willcocks’s calculations to claim that well irrigation allowed the summer sorghum crop to be grown on only 10 per cent of the land. The other 90 per cent would be unused in summer, ‘owing to the scarcity of labour’.

This calculation made the old system appear less productive. Leaving aside the fact that steam pumps could replace human and animal labour to lift well water in flood basins, a development already under way, labour was scarce for two reasons, one of which we will come to below.

But the immediate cause, as Willcocks himself explained, was the emptying of men from villages in the south to provide labour in the north, to excavate and maintain the system of canals on which cotton cultivation now depended, driven there by the imposition of forced labour or hired on contracts paid from public funds.
In other words, the
extraordinary need for labour that made the new canal system in the north so expensive was used perversely to make the
system appear impractical.

zh: 四年后，在苏格兰地理学会的一次演讲中，罗斯承认水井灌溉是合适的，但只适合小耕作者：“要引入甘蔗、棉花或水稻等夏季作物，”他承认，“我们首先只需挖井，用机器把水提上来。”然而他坚持认为，这种方法“适合拥有小块土地、以自给自足方式生活的耕作者。它不经济，也不能以最少劳动获得最大产量。”他或许是在暗指苏丹——如前所述，那里水车仍被广泛使用，马赫迪国家曾击败埃及占领——补充说：“对于半野蛮国家，容易因战争和半野蛮敌人的入侵而动荡，这种方法极好。”他甚至承认：“上埃及仍有许多地区以这种方式耕作，井水实际上取之不尽，因为即使在夏季，尼罗河水面距地表也从不超过 35 英尺。”然而，他认为，要大规模进行夏季种植，必须用由地表运河和蒸汽泵组成的系统取代地下水的使用。
en: Four years later, in a lecture to the Scottish Geographical Society, Ross conceded that irrigation using wells was suitable, but only for small cultivators: ‘To introduce summer crops, such as sugar, cotton, or rice,’ he acknowledged, ‘we have only, in the first instance, to dig wells and lift up the water by machines.’ He insisted, however, that this method ‘is suitable to cultivators who have small holdings, and who live in a self-supporting fashion. It is not economical, nor is there a maximum of produce for a minimum of labour expended.’ Alluding, perhaps, to Sudan, where waterwheels (as noted) were still widely used and the Mahdist state had defeated the Egyptian occupation, he added, ‘For semi-barbaric countries, liable to be upset by war and incursions of semi-savage enemies, it is excellent.’ He even admitted that ‘There are still many tracts of Upper Egypt cultivated thus, and the well-water is practically inexhaustible, as the Nile-water is never more than 35 feet below the surface even in summer.’ However, for summer cultivation on a large scale, he argued, the use of groundwater must be replaced by a system of surface canals and steam pumps.

zh: 我们必须把尼罗河水引到地表，办法要么是修建运河，要么是在尼罗河上游很远的地方开凿一条坡度平缓的引水渠，要么用蒸汽动力把水抽到田地高度或抽入一条大运河，要么在尼罗河中筑坝，抬高其夏季水位，使开挖运河的成本不至于过高。
en: We must bring the water of the Nile to the surface, either by a canal or a low-grade slope taking off far up the Nile, or by pumping water by steam power up to the field level or into a large canal, or we must make a dam in the Nile to raise its summer level, so that the cost of excavating the canal may not be excessive.

zh: 《埃及灌溉》后来的版本降低了对
系统的强调，把关于水井使用的论述主要限制在“埃及土壤”的初步观察中。当报告转入灌溉的详细讨论时，焦点是洪水控制以及运河和拦河堰的建设。
到 1908 年，福阿登和弗莱彻的《埃及农业教科书》——由教育部在国立大学创立之年在开罗出版——直截了当地指出：“在围堤蓄水制度下，只能种植冬季作物……在收获与洪水之间没有农活可做。”
使用地下水的井灌系统被弄得不可见。埃及的农业史和经济史如今可以书写了，只是缺少了一半图景。
en: The later editions of
reduced the emphasis on the

system, confining remarks on the use of wells mainly to preliminary observations on ‘The Soil of Egypt’. When the report moved on to the detailed discussion of irrigation, the focus was on flood control and the construction of canals and barrages.
By 1908, Foaden and Fletcher’s

, published in Cairo by the Ministry of Education in the year of the founding of a national university, stated flatly that ‘under the basin system, only winter crops can be grown . . . There is no agricultural work to be done between harvest and flood.’
The system of well irrigation using subterranean water was rendered invisible. Egypt’s agrarian and economic history could now be written, with half the picture missing.

zh: 畜力
en: Animal Power

zh: 除了在政府登记簿中缺席以及英国人想消除它之外，历史叙述忽视这个系统的第三个原因，可能在于大多数欧洲作家只看到了它的残迹。

就像十六世纪登陆秘鲁的西班牙征服者，发现印加世界已因先期抵达的天花而陷入崩溃一样，穆罕默德·阿里治下的法国工程师以及后来取代他们的英国人，遇到的是一个遭受一系列流行病和大流行病袭击的国家，这些疾病在欧洲军队之前就已传到埃及。尽管没有可靠数字，1800 年埃及人口可能处于几个世纪以来的最低点，饱受周期性鼠疫爆发和新出现的霍乱威胁之苦。俄罗斯向北方的奥斯曼领土扩张，英国和法国在东地中海及南亚扩张军事势力，由此带来的战争增多，以及贸易和朝圣往来的日益频繁，都促使这两种疾病传播。
穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者在奥斯曼早先公共卫生政策的基础上，实行隔离和其他措施，使人口水平得以恢复，但霍乱和鼠疫在 1830 年代再次袭击，霍乱也频繁重现，包括 1881 年英国占领前夕。
欧洲人倾向于把鼠疫和其他疾病视为病态东方的自然特征，视为界定其与西方差异的一部分，而不是视为暴力、动荡和交换加剧的产物，尽管他们自己在其中扮演了主导角色。
因此，在他们看来使现有耕作方法无利可图的“劳动力稀缺”，不仅是由于劳动密集型的运河灌溉棉花生产增加，也是帝国扩张和战争的长期影响所致。
en: A third reason why historical accounts have ignored this system, besides its absence from government registers and the British desire to eliminate it, may be that most European writers saw only its vestiges.

Like the Spanish conquistadores landing in sixteenth-century Peru and finding an Inca world already collapsing from the smallpox that had reached there ahead of them, the French engineers under Muhammad Ali and the British who later replaced them encountered a country attacked by a series of epidemic and pandemic diseases that had travelled to Egypt in advance of the European forces. Although we have no reliable figures, in 1800 the population of Egypt may have been at its lowest point in centuries, afflicted by periodic outbreaks of plague and by the new threat of cholera. Both diseases spread with the increased warfare that came with Russian expansion into Ottoman lands to the north and British and French military expansion in the Eastern Mediterranean and South Asia, as well as the increasing movement of trade and pilgrimage traffic.

Building on earlier Ottoman public health policy, Muhammad Ali and his successors introduced quarantines and other measures that allowed population levels to recover, but epidemics of cholera and plague struck again in the 1830s, and cholera reappeared frequently, including in 1881, on the eve of the British occupation.

Europeans tended to see plague and other diseases as a natural aspect of a sickly Orient, part of what defined its difference from the West, rather than as the product of forms of violence, upheaval, and intensification of exchange in which they themselves played a leading role.

So the ‘scarcity of labour’ that, in their view, rendered existing methods of cultivation unprofitable was caused not only by an increase in the more labour-intensive method of canal-irrigated cotton production, but by longer-term effects of imperial expansion and warfare.
body.review: 校注：底本写1881年英国占领前夕霍乱再次出现，原注109所引论文题名则为1883年疫情。该注另引Kuhnke的Lives at Risk区分了1881年汉志霍乱及埃及检疫措施，与1883年埃及疫情。正文照录，不将两地与两年混同。 https://publishing.cdlib.org/ucpressebooks/public/book/lives-at-risk-public-health-in-nineteenth-century-egypt.html

zh: 即使防治鼠疫和霍乱的措施降低了发病率，另一种疾病更直接地影响了使用
的井灌。它攻击这个系统的主要动力——该国的牛群。这就是牛瘟，一种针对消化道的传染病，引起发烧和大面积胃肠炎，产生“令人作呕的恶臭”，在多数情况下导致死亡。在最严重的形式中，它可以杀死所感染动物的 95% 以上。
en: Even as measures to combat plague and cholera reduced their incidence, another disease affected more directly the employment of well irrigation using

. It attacked the main motor of the system, the country’s cattle population. This was rinderpest, the cattle plague, a contagious disease that targets the digestive tract causing fever and extensive gastroenteritis, producing a ‘loathsome stench’ and, in most cases, death. In its severest form, it can kill more than 95 per cent of the animals it afflicts.

zh: 现代时期第一次大动物流行病暴发于 1784—5 年，使埃及南部的牲畜大批死亡。在接下来的四年里，它又三次袭击开罗和
北方。政府敦促农民改用水牛而不是黄牛来转动水车。
在许多情况下，人们不得不代替死去的动物，用自己的身体转动水车。
1820 年代，政府组织从苏丹中部的科尔多凡进口黄牛，以应对持续的短缺。
没有动物，水井便被废弃。1826 年，穆罕默德·阿里帕夏向他负责尼罗河三角洲西部米努夫和阿什蒙两个区的官员抱怨，该区的“水井和水车结构失修”。
1833 年，帕夏设立了一个政府办事处，从苏丹进口替换牲畜，在尼罗河畔的基纳修建大型牲口棚，牛只从南方运到那里。
病毒在 1841—2 年再次袭击，从俄罗斯草原经多瑙河和的里雅斯特传来，摧毁了该国多达 90% 的牛群。
1861 年和 1863—4 年，南方又爆发了疫情。当地报告说，一些地方每天损失三四百头牛，农民“因缺少牛而无法浇地”，社区虚弱得无法搬走和掩埋所有尸体，成千上万头死牛顺河漂流。人们再一次“用自己的身体转动萨基亚水车”。
据记载，1872—6 年和 1881 年英国占领前夕又发生了疫情。最后，1889 年爆发了牛瘟大流行，它始于埃塞俄比亚，当时意大利军队正从厄立特里亚海岸扩大殖民占领。
这场瘟疫沿非洲大陆南北蔓延近十年，在埃及及其南方国家造成毁灭性后果。
en: The first major epizootic of the modern period struck in 1784–5, decimating the livestock of southern Egypt. It returned in Cairo and the
north three times in the next four years. The government urged farmers to respond by using water buffalo instead of oxen to turn the water-wheels.
In many cases humans had to replace the dead animals, turning the waterwheels with their own bodies.
In the 1820s, the government organised the importing of oxen from Kordofan in central Sudan to deal with the continuing shortage.

Without animals, the wells fell into disuse. In 1826, Muhammad Ali Pasha complained to his official in charge of Minuf and Ashmoun, two western districts of the Nile Delta, that the district’s ‘wells and waterwheel structures are in disrepair’.
In 1833 the Pasha set up a government office for importing replacement cattle from Sudan, building large barns on the Nile at Qina, where the animals arrived from the south.
The virus struck again in 1841–2, arriving from the Russian steppes via the Danube and Trieste, and destroying as much as 90 per cent of the country’s herds.

In 1861 and 1863–4, there were outbreaks in the south. Local reports speak of some localities losing three or four hundred head of cattle a day, farmers ‘unable to water the land for want of oxen’, communities too weak to carry off and bury all the carcasses, and dead cattle flowing down the river in their thousands. Once again, ‘men [we]re turning the sakiahs’ with their own bodies.

Further outbreaks were recorded in 1872–6 and in 1881 on the eve of the British occupation. Finally, there arrived the great rinderpest panzootic of 1889, which started in Ethiopia as Italian forces expanded their colonial occupation from the coast of Eritrea.
The plague spread north and south along the length of the continent for almost a decade, with devastating consequences in Egypt and the countries to its south.

zh: 在埃塞俄比亚，由此引发的饥荒——因连续三年厄尔尼诺相关干旱而加剧——是有记忆以来最严重的一次。
牛的损失消除了主要的热能来源——干牛粪，给本已稀少的木材供应带来压力。到该世纪最后十年，埃塞俄比亚高原的树木覆盖——已因农业扩张而减少，又因奥斯曼—埃及、英国和意大利军队的入侵而进一步受损——降至最低点。
土地失去树木，促成了降雨量、降雨强度以及河流径流的变化。径流成为尼罗河的洪水，而洪水又因此变得更加极端，时而过高，时而过低。因此，牛瘟可能在埃及产生了第二重影响：它不仅反复摧毁畜力系统，同时也使这些动物用水车提取的洪水变得更加多变和不可预测。
en: In Ethiopia, the resulting famine, exacerbated by three years of El Niño–related droughts, was the worst in memory.

The loss of cattle removed the main source of heat energy, dried cow dung, putting pressure on scarce supplies of timber. By the last decade of the century, tree cover across the Ethiopian highlands, already reduced by agricultural expansion and further damaged by the invasion of Ottoman-Egyptian, British, and Italian armies, was at its lowest.

Denuding the land of its trees contributed to changes in the level and intensity of rainfall and runoff into rivers. The runoff becomes the flood waters of the Nile, which, in turn, saw more extreme high and low floods. So, the cattle plague may have had a second impact in Egypt: as well as repeatedly destroying the system of animal power, it simultaneously made the flood waters that those animals lifted using waterwheels more variable and unpredictable.

zh: 当英国工程师在 1880 年代和 1890 年代调查并记述他们所看到的灌溉系统时，以及此前几十年的法国工程师也是如此，他们目睹的是一套机制，其关键部件和主要能源已被反复攻击和摧毁。
en: When British engineers surveyed and wrote about the irrigation system as they found it in the 1880s and 1890s, and French engineers in the decades before them, they were witnessing a mechanism whose vital parts and main source of energy had been repeatedly attacked and destroyed.

zh: 所谓饥荒史
en: The So-Called History of Famines

zh: 英国当局急于为殖民重新工程化河流和对河流的生态破坏辩护，忽视了最近的流行病和动物流行病史——他们自己的帝国行动和其他欧洲强国的行动对这种历史负有责任——也忽视了地下蓄水系统，而这个系统曾调节供水，并创造了肥沃而适应性强的耕作制度。他们忽视了边缘土地作为泄水区的用途，那里可以储存多余的水，供洪水大的年份使用。他们排除了埃及主要工程师阿里·穆巴拉克的建议，即更多地利用这类水库，作为在河流筑坝的替代方案。
他们还拒绝了瓦迪拉扬计划——一位美国考古学家提出的项目，旨在恢复法尤姆附近一个古老湖泊，以储存多余的灌溉水，作为三角洲拦河堰的替代方案。
en: Anxious to justify the colonial re-engineering and ecological destruction of the river, the British authorities overlooked the recent history of epidemics and epizootics to which their own imperial actions and those of other European powers had contributed and ignored the system of subterranean water storage that had regulated the supply of water and created a fertile and adaptable system of farming. They ignored the use of marginal lands as an escape, in which excess water could be stored and used in years of high floods. They ruled out the proposals of the leading Egyptian engineer, Ali Mubarak, to increase the use of such reservoirs as an alternative to the damming of the river.

They also rejected the Wadi Rayan scheme, the project of an American archaeologist to restore an ancient lake adjacent to Fayyum to store excess irrigation waters, as an alternative to the Delta Barrage.

zh: 此外，随着殖民政权以永久运河和拦河堰为基础，巩固对河流更集中的控制，一个新的无知空间打开了。电报的使用使官员能够从开罗监测洪水威胁，开始害怕这种“风险”。以前在当地处理的计算与决策，如今要在远处作出。

过去在洪水高涨时，当上涨的尼罗河接近峰值，巡堤人会被部署在堤岸的脆弱地段，并由一群准备处理任何决口的人协助；河面上布满装载石头和木桩的小船，供修复之用，所有船上都挂着灯笼。灯光倒映在水中，“场景充满欢快与生气，”一位英国地区工程师在这样一个地点报道说，“陌生人会以为正在举行盛大的集市。”这位工程师赞赏处理任何威胁时“沉稳而务实的作风”，并“觉得几乎不可能发生决口，而开罗的官员坐在办公室里读着电报副本，总是紧张胆怯”。
en: In addition, as the colonial regime consolidated a more centralised control of the river, based on permanent canals and barrages, a new space of ignorance opened up. The use of the telegraph allowed officials to monitor the threat of flooding from Cairo, becoming fearful of the ‘risk’. Calculations and decisions that were previously handled locally were now to be made at a distance.

In the past, during high floods, when the rising Nile approached its peak, watchmen would be stationed along vulnerable stretches of the embankment, assisted by gangs of men ready to deal with any breach, while the river was covered with small boats laden with stones and stakes for making repairs, all carrying lanterns. With the lamps reflected in the water, ‘the scene is full of gaiety and animation’, reported a British district engineer at one such site. ‘A stranger might imagine a great fair was on.’ Admiring the ‘steady business-like manner’ in which any threat was addressed, the engineer ‘felt that it was almost impossible for a breach to occur, while the officials in Cairo, seated in their offices reading the duplicates of telegrams, were always nervous and timid’.

zh: 所谓旧制度的脆弱性，部分正是消除它的措施所制造的无知的产物。从开罗的
办公室，英国高级官员把过去几个世纪的尼罗河灌溉描绘成一个人类极不安全的系统，国家的生存始终面临河流不可预测性以及生态破坏和饥荒威胁的风险。官员们还把这种不可预测性归咎于对殖民统治的抵抗，包括 1881 年在马赫迪穆罕默德·艾哈迈德·本·阿卜杜拉领导下在苏丹建立独立国家。“德尔维希（苦行僧派）阻止对尼罗河流量的任何科学考察，”他们抱怨道。
河流控制将成为消除这种独立的论据。一条不驯之河的生态和政治“风险”，被一群不驯的民众放大，成为进一步摧毁这条河的理由。
en: The alleged vulnerability of the old system was partly a product of the very ignorance produced by the measures to eliminate it. From their

offices in Cairo, senior British officials pictured Nile irrigation over the preceding centuries as a system of great human precarity, in which the very survival of the country was permanently at risk from the river’s unpredictability and the ever-present threat of ecological devastation and famine. The officials also blamed this unpredictability on resistance to colonial rule, including the establishing of an independent state in Sudan in 1881 under the Mahdi, Muhammad Ahmad bin Abd Allah. ‘The Dervishes’, they complained, ‘prevent any scientific examination’ of the flow of the Nile.

River control would become an argument for the elimination of such independence. The ecological and political ‘risk’ of an unruly river, magnified by an unruly population, was a further justification for the river’s destruction.

zh: 这种关于不稳定的观点在大多数现代历史叙述中被复制，为弑河行为提供了托词。它又因对早期阿拉伯作家的误读而得到强化。
基于同时代资料的中世纪埃及史提供了不同的图景。由于尼罗河在赤道东非有众多源头，埃塞俄比亚季风又十分规律，它的洪水节律比世界上任何其他河流都更可预测、更可靠。
虽然洪水峰顶的高度和时间逐年变化，但一旦水位开始上涨，这种变化就可以预测——例如，记录洪峰之间的间隔以及尼罗河沿岸测量站冲积沉积物的密度。
根据这些预测，可以扩大或缩小耕种面积，还可以像前面提到的那样，把多余的水储存在泄水区，或通过井灌在第二季甚至第三季种植额外作物，以应对低水位洪水。如果到第三季水井水位下降，次年夏天上涨的尼罗河会补给它们。
有丰年也有荒年，但极端情况因以下能力而得到缓和：把谷物和豆类从一个季节储存到下一个季节，无论是存放在住宅内，还是储存在大商人和统治家族的粮仓中，后者可能拥有数千甚至数万吨粮食。
慈善基金会（阿拉伯语
，单数
）拥有大片土地，这些土地发展成一种保护城乡财产免受政府征税要求的工具；它们利用粮食储备和厨房，在短缺时期支持弱势者。
该国的纺织品生产——主要建立在种植亚麻、织成亚麻布的基础上，这一行业在中世纪繁荣，并在十七和
十八世纪复兴——提供了又一种储存系统。
亚麻在低洼地带的湿润土壤中茁壮生长，使人们能够利用大洪水留下的多余土地，并把剩余物储存起来。
亚麻工业的扩张可能部分出于这个目的，同时商人也从为其生产提供预付信贷中获利。把田地作物变成一匹匹布，提供了比谷物更安全、更有价值、更耐久、也更具可互换性的财富储存手段。事实上，成卷的布匹比粮仓更容易被用来隐匿财富以逃税，甚至可能被用来缴税。
由于能够储存谷物、豆类、织物和洪水，在中世纪埃及，洪水脉冲的波动从未导致饥荒。
en: This view of precarity is reproduced in most modern historical accounts, providing an alibi for the act of rivercide. It has been reinforced by a misreading of earlier Arab writers.

Histories of medieval Egypt, based on contemporaneous sources, offer a different picture. The flood regime of the Nile was more predictable and more dependable than that of any other world river, thanks to the multiplicity of its sources in equatorial East Africa and the regularity of the Ethiopian monsoon.

While the height and timing of the crest of the flood varied from year to year, the variation could be predicted once the water levels began to rise – for example, by recording the interval between surges and the density of the alluvium deposit at measuring stations along the Nile.

The area to be cultivated could be extended or restricted based on these predictions, with the further options, as mentioned, of storing excess water in escapes or dealing with low floods by planting additional crops using well-water irrigation in a second and even a third season. If by the third season the wells were running low, the rising Nile of the following summer replenished them.

There were years of abundance and years of scarcity, but the extremes were moderated by the ability to store grains and pulses from one season to the next, whether within the domestic dwelling or in the granaries of large merchants and the ruling households, who might hold thousands or in some cases tens of thousands of tons.
Charitable foundations (in Arabic,
, or

, singular), whose extensive landholdings developed as a means of shielding rural and urban property from the government’s revenue claims, used their food stores and kitchens to support the disadvantaged in periods of shortage.
The country’s textile production, based mainly on growing flax to weave into linen, an industry that flourished in the medieval period and was revived again in the seventeenth and
eighteenth centuries, provided a further storage system.
Thriving in the moist soil of low-lying tracts, flax allowed the utilisation of surplus land from a heavy flood, and the storing of the surplus.

The flax industry may have expanded partly for this purpose, alongside the profit that merchants made from advancing credit for its production. Transforming a field crop into bolts of cloth provided a means of storing wealth that was more secure, valuable, durable, and fungible even than grain. In fact, rolls of cloth could be used more easily than granaries to secrete wealth to avoid the payment of taxes, and may even have been used to pay those taxes.
Thanks to the ability to store grain, pulses, fabrics, and flood water, in medieval Egypt the fluctuation in the flood pulse was never a cause of famine.

zh: 前现代时期生计的主要威胁不是河流的多变，而是偶尔发生的政治动荡，例如 1062—73 年的“大灾难”（
），或十二世纪末和十三世纪末的政治危机。
更常见的是来自大商人的威胁，他们受诱在预期短缺时囤积粮食，以抬高价格。他们有时夸大洪水峰顶偏低的威胁，使民众恐慌购买，从而为其涨价提供理由。
马穆鲁克时期关于这些问题的主要史料是马格里齐约 1405 年写的
，它按时间顺序记载了此前几个世纪每一次已知的粮食短缺和困苦。它承认气候因素在洪水变化和粮食生产中的作用。它顺带提到两个世纪前一个离奇的记载：干旱极端严重，以至于富人开始食用儿童的血肉，并“对此习以为常”。
但这本书主要论述政府当局和市场监督官（
）控制价格、惩罚欺诈的责任；马格里齐本人曾三次为开罗城担任这一职务。他把近期的匮乏归因于当局决定停止铸造银币，转而依靠账面信用（记账货币），辅以作为辅币的铜币；马格里齐指责这种做法贬低货币价值，使农民贫困。
en: The main threat to livelihoods in the pre-modern period came not from the variability of the river but from occasional episodes of political strife, as with the ‘great calamity’ (
) of 1062–73, or the political crises at the end of the twelfth century and again at the end of the thirteenth.

More frequently, the threat came from large merchants, who were tempted to hoard supplies of grain in anticipation of shortages in order to drive up the price. They would sometimes exaggerate the threat of a low crest to the flood, to panic the population into purchases that would justify their raising of prices.
The principal historical source on these matters from the Mamluk period, Maqrizi’s

, written around 1405, chronicles every known episode over the preceding centuries of food shortage and distress. It acknowledges the role of climatic factors in the variation of the flood and grain production. It mentions in passing a fantastical account from two centuries earlier of a drought so extreme that the well-to-do began to consume the flesh of children, a taste ‘to which they became accustomed’.
But the text addresses mainly the responsibility of government authorities and the market supervisor, or

, an office in which Maqrizi himself served for the city of Cairo on three occasions, to control prices and punish fraud. He attributes recent episodes of dearth to the decision of the authorities to cease coining money in silver and rely instead on book credit (money of account) supplemented with token copper coins, a practice Maqrizi blames for debasing the value of money and impoverishing the peasantry.

zh: 马格里齐这本书的押韵书名很难译成英文，但可以译为《考察困苦以救助民众》。最早注意到这部著作的法国东方学家给它起了另一个书名：
把这本书称为“关于
饥荒的论著”，并未抓住马格里齐文本的含义及其对货币和信用的关切（这个主题我们将在下一章讨论），反而抓住了殖民者对农业危机的执念。所谓的饥荒“风险”确立了旧秩序的不足和脆弱，为有计划地摧毁河流提供了又一个托词。
en: The rhymed title of Maqrizi’s book is difficult to render in English but can be translated as ‘Aiding the Community by Examining Its Distress’. The French Orientalists who first noted the work’s existence gave it a different title:
Calling the book a ‘treatise on

famines’ captured not the meaning of Maqrizi’s text and its concern with money and credit (a topic to which we turn in the next chapter) but the colonial preoccupation with agrarian crisis. The supposed ‘risk’ of famine established the inadequacy and precarity of the old order and provided a further alibi for the planned destruction of the river.

zh: 资本化
en: Capitalisation

zh: 关注地表水而忽视灌溉水的储存和提取方法，还有另一个原因。建立在地表水和地下水储存基础上的旧方法——畜力、多季种植——对于农业如今要服务的新目的来说适应性过强、过于复杂。尼罗河的殖民化和资本化无法轻易与洪水退去后的农业制度共存，不是因为土地需要生产更多——正如我们将看到的，土地生产力即将迅速下降——而是因为它需要以不同方式生产，这种方式把泛滥从资源变成威胁。殖民主义如今将设计出一个“易受洪水侵害的景观”，其风险更适合于从未来抽取，而不是对自然的开发。
en: Focusing on surface water and ignoring the methods of storing and lifting irrigation water had an additional reason. The old methods of animal-powered, multiple cropping, based on both surface and subterranean storage, were too adaptable and too complex for the novel purpose that agriculture was now to serve. The colonising and capitalising of the Nile could not easily coexist with the regime of flood-recession farming, not because the land needed to produce more – as we will see, the productivity of the land was set to rapidly decline – but because it needed to produce differently, in ways that turned inundation from a resource into a threat. Colonialism would now engineer a ‘flood-vulnerable landscape’, one whose risks were better suited, not to the exploitation of nature, but to extraction from the future.

zh: 在英国殖民主义下，尼罗河将作为从未来获利——通过征税——的手段运作。从未来抽取支付的机制本身并不新鲜。几个世纪以来，开罗的大商人依靠向耕作者提供信贷而兴旺，办法是签订预购作物合同，待交货时以更高价格出售。定期缴税的要求帮助迫使耕地者预售产品并负债。征税的当局和为缴税预付信贷的商人相互依赖，以充实自身。近几个世纪，在马穆鲁克和奥斯曼统治下，特定村庄及其土地税收份额的权利被作为薪饷分配给军官，后来又拍卖给包税人。这些收入权利演变为乡村庄园，使其持有者成为商人和耕作者之间抽取机制的中介。十九世纪初，穆罕默德·阿里用直接征税取代包税制，试图通过命令把作物直接运到政府仓库来排挤大商人，随后开始把未来收成、并逐渐把整个庄园
作为信用支付分配给外国商人，作为对扩张中的军队和农村行政的军官和官员的补偿。控制这些庄园——其中许多从旧马穆鲁克统治家族手中没收——的人，被指定为“负责者”（
），负责向政府缴纳所欠税款，而政府逐渐提高并简化了税率。
en: The Nile under British colonialism was to operate as a means of profiting from – by taxing – the future. Mechanisms for extracting payments from the future were not in themselves something new. For centuries, the large merchants of Cairo had prospered from the ability to extend credit to cultivators, through contracts for the advance purchase of crops that they could sell for a higher price when delivered. The requirement to pay taxes at regular intervals helped compel those who farmed the land to sell their produce in advance and become indebted. The authorities imposing taxes and the merchants advancing credit for their payment depended on one another for their own enrichment. In recent centuries, under Mamluk and Ottoman rule, the right to a share in the tax revenues of specific villages and their lands had been assigned as salaries to military officers and later auctioned to tax farmers. These rights to revenue evolved into rural estates, inserting the holders as middlemen between merchants and cultivators in the mechanism of extraction. In the early nineteenth century, Muhammad Ali replaced tax farming with direct taxation, tried to cut out the large merchants by commanding the delivery of crops directly to government warehouses, and then began allocating future harvests, and gradually entire estates,

as credit payments to foreign merchants and as recompense for the military officers and officials of an expanding army and rural administration. Those controlling the estates, many of which were confiscated from the former Mamluk ruling households, were made ‘responsible’ (
) for the taxes owed to the government, which gradually raised and simplified the tax rate.

zh: 正如阿姆尔·海勒·艾哈迈德（Amr Khairy Ahmed）所解释的，在该世纪下半叶，两场危机帮助产生了新规模的资本化。第一，一波接一波的牛瘟消灭了驱动该国灌溉机械的畜力，为引入大量以赊购方式供应的蒸汽泵创造了机会。牛是通过合作安排或合伙关系饲养、喂养和繁殖的，这些安排很少提供抽取信用支付的机会；而蒸汽泵成本高得多、寿命长得多，使贷款得以激增，包括为购买进口煤炭而提供的贷款。第二，美国以奴隶制为基础的棉花生产的持续，引发了另一场危机：美国内战和 1861—5 年的全球棉花饥荒。它与埃及 1863—4 年的牛瘟同时发生，棉价的跳升为该国的欧洲和黎凡特金融家提供了以新规模创造信用的手段。
蒸汽动力轧棉机与灌溉泵一起，成为资本化的机器。当棉花饥荒突然结束时，赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔转向糖业生产；他从 1863 年统治到 1879 年在欧洲债权人及其政府的要求下被废黜。他下令开挖该国最长的运河——中埃及的易卜拉希米亚运河——为其配备大型蒸汽泵站以灌溉广阔的甘蔗种植园，并建造“由蒸汽驱动的大型制糖厂，在厂中碾磨甘蔗并完成煮沸和精炼”。
机械、基础设施和种植园的规模，促成了甚至更大规模的信用创造。伊斯梅尔所借贷款的一半到四分之三，用于购买蒸汽泵并为新种植园建造工厂、轻便铁路、运河和其他基础设施。
伊斯梅尔日益独立于伊斯坦布尔，使金融家能够通过抵押政府收入，最终抵押整个政府和王室地产来获得信用保障。到 1870 年代末，这些国家和王室领地——如今已被宣布伊斯梅尔破产的欧洲债权人夺取和管理——占该国耕地面积的 10%。
种植园和机械、它们所设计的债务水平，以及它们促成的生态、
金融和政治危机，触发了英国占领。伊斯梅尔及其债权人在该国糖业和棉花种植园中开创的做法，如今要在全国范围内尝试。
en: In the second half of the century, as Amr Khairy Ahmed explains, two crises helped generate a new scale of capitalisation. First, waves of cattle plague, wiping out the animal power that drove the country’s irrigation machinery, created the opportunity to introduce large numbers of steam-driven pumps, supplied on credit. While cattle were raised, nourished, and reproduced through collaborative arrangements or partnerships that seldom provided openings for extracting credit payments, the much greater cost and longevity of a steam pump allowed a proliferation of loans, including those provided to purchase imports of coal. Second, the perpetuation of slave-based cotton production in the United States triggered another crisis, the American Civil War and the worldwide cotton famine of 1861–5. Coinciding with the 1863–4 cattle plague in Egypt, the jump in cotton prices offered the country’s European and Levantine financiers the means to create credit on a new scale.

Steam-powered cotton gins joined the irrigation pumps as machineries of capitalisation. When the cotton famine abruptly ended, Khedive Isma‘il, who ruled from 1863 until his deposition at the behest of his European creditors and their governments in 1879, switched to sugar production. He commissioned the digging of the country’s longest canal, the Ibrahimiya Canal in Middle Egypt, equipped it with large steam-powered pumping stations to feed extensive cane plantations, and built ‘immense sugar manufactories worked by steam, in which the cane is ground and the boiling and refining done’.

The size of the machinery, infrastructure, and plantations facilitated an even larger creation of credit. Between half and three-quarters of the loans that Isma‘il took on were used to purchase steam pumps and build factories, light railways, canals, and other infrastructure for the new plantations.

The increasing independence of Isma‘il from Istanbul allowed the financiers to secure the credit through mortgages on government revenues and eventually on entire government and royal estates. By the end of the 1870s these state and royal domains, now seized and administered by the European creditors who had declared Isma‘il bankrupt, occupied 10 per cent of the country’s cultivated area.
The plantations and machinery, the levels of debt they engineered, and the ecological,

financial, and political crises to which they contributed triggered the British occupation. What Isma‘il and his creditors had pioneered on the country’s sugar and cotton plantations was now to be attempted across the country as a whole.

zh: 要进一步扩大从未来抽取的系统，就需要以不同方式储水：不再使用围堤田块及其下方的地层，也不使用少数几条深挖的夏季运河（它们依赖同一地下水的渗流），而是把水储存在一个大型地表水库中、河流本身因水位抬高而增大的水体中，以及工业作物的纤维素壁中。
en: Expanding further the system of extraction from the future required water to be stored differently: rather than using field basins and the substrate beneath them, and the handful of deeply excavated summer canals, which depended on seepage from the same groundwater, storage was to be located in a large surface reservoir, in the raised volume of the river itself, and within the cellulose walls of industrial crops.

zh: 为了以新规模使埃及农业资本化，把尼罗河本身变成一台信用和时间转移的机器，金融家力图扩大棉花和甘蔗这两种工业作物的种植，而这两者都不受小农欢迎。工业作物不在当地消费，也不能留待将来使用。农户和商人可以把谷物、豆类、稻米和当地加工的纺织纤维储存数年，却难以储存棉花或甘蔗。收获时，整批作物迅速离开本地人手中，运往糖厂或轧棉厂。
作物种植与其产品的加工、制造之间的分离，使种植者保留的作物价值份额更容易被削减。传统上保留大部分主食作物的农民，从经济作物中获得的收入可能不到其价值的一半。不归耕作者的那部分价值如今可以通过出售土地所有权提供给投资者，成为一种可被资本化的长期未来收入。
en: To capitalise Egyptian agriculture on a new scale, turning the Nile itself into a machine of credit and time transfer, financiers sought to expand the growing of the two industrial crops, cotton and sugar cane, neither of which was popular among small farmers. Industrial crops are not consumed locally and cannot be set aside for future use. While farming households and merchants can store cereal grains, pulses, rice, and locally processed textile fibres for years, they cannot easily store cotton or sugar cane. At harvest, the entire crop moves quickly out of local hands and is carried to sugar mills or cotton gins.

The interruption between the growing of the crop and the processing and manufacturing of its product made it easier to reduce the share of the crop’s value retained by the grower. Farmers who conventionally kept a large part of a staple food crop might receive less than half the value of crops grown for manufacturing. The non-farming share could now be made available to investors, via the sale of title to the land, becoming a longterm future income to be capitalised.

zh: 由于与工业用途相关的种种原因，大规模种植的工业作物与现有的蓄水系统不相容，因而也与尼罗河的生命周期不相容。它们需要不同的种植期，基于获取灌溉水的不同时间表。大多数基本粮食作物生长很快——食物通常储存在果实或种子中，播种后几周内即可收获。
在全年日照和灌溉水（来自洪水和井水）的环境中，正如我们所见，这使一年种植多季作物成为可能。相比之下，这两种工业作物的价值不在于快速生长的果实或种子，而在于其支撑结构的纤维素组织——储存甘蔗汁液的茎秆，或容纳棉株棉纤维的棉铃。
这种纤维素储存容器的成熟需要长得多的时间。长绒棉占地九
个月，甘蔗长达十二个月，还要加上犁地和整地所需的数周，因此每年只能种一季。旧的双层灌溉水储存系统要求在夏末让大部分田地被淹长达六周。工业作物需要长达一年时间来构建自己的储存系统，无法与洪水周期同步。
en: For reasons related to their industrial purpose, industrial crops grown on an extensive scale were incompatible with the existing system of water storage, and thus incompatible with the life cycle of the Nile. They required a different period of cultivation, based on a different timetable of access to irrigation water. Most basic food crops grow quickly – the food is typically stored in the fruit or seed, which can be ready to harvest within a few weeks of sowing.

In an environment with year-round sunshine and irrigation water, from flood water and well water, this allowed, as we have seen, the growing of multiple crops in a year. The value of the two industrial crops, in contrast, lies not in a fast-growing fruit or seed, but in the cellulosic structure of its support – the stalk that stores the juices of the sugar cane or the boll that contains the lint of the cotton plant.
This cellulose storage vessel takes much longer to mature. Long-staple cotton occupies the ground for nine

months and sugar cane for up to twelve, in addition to the weeks needed for ploughing and preparing the soil, allowing for only one crop per year. The old double-layered system for storing irrigation water required the flooding of most fields for up to six weeks in late summer. The industrial crops, needing up to a year to build their own storage system, could not be synchronised with the flood cycle.

zh: 始终可以留出小块土地种植甘蔗和棉花，以及第三种夏季工业作物靛蓝植物，用水车从井中或上涨的河水中灌溉。
在中世纪和近代早期，对大商人来说，这些作物较长的生长期不是障碍，而是其利润的来源。棉花通常限于一英亩或一英亩半的小块地，而乡间的围堤田区延伸数百或数千英亩。
甘蔗的种植更为广泛。大约从十一世纪起，埃及利用水车灌溉小块土地，发展出重要的制糖业。糖被视为药物，早期榨糖厂的投资者往往是医生。
据内莉·汉纳所述，十七世纪对甘蔗种植有了新的投资，到该世纪末，糖的精炼和贸易已成为开罗最赚钱的生意之一。
对大商人来说，甘蔗的优势恰恰在于其生长季的长度。从种植到收获之间长达一年的延迟，迫使农民预售作物以借债，为缴税和其他需求提供资金。对于很大一部分利润来自提供信贷的商人来说（我们将在下一章进一步探讨），生长季越长，潜在利润就越大。
出于同样的原因，大多数农民避免种植甘蔗，因为“种植它需要预付资金”。
en: It was always feasible to reserve small sections of land for cane and cotton, along with the third industrial summer crop, indigo, to be irrigated from wells or from the rising river using waterwheels.

In the medieval and early modern period, for large merchants, the extended growing season of these crops was not a handicap but a source of their profitability. Cotton was generally restricted to small plots of an acre or an acre and a half, in a countryside where field basins extended for hundreds or thousands of acres.

Sugar cane was more extensively cultivated. From around the eleventh century, Egypt developed an important sugar industry using irrigation of small tracts by waterwheel. The sugar was valued as a medicine, and the investors in early cane-pressing factories were often physicians.

In the seventeenth century, according to Nelly Hanna, there was a renewed investment in sugar cultivation and, by the end of that century, the refining and trading of sugar was one of Cairo’s most profitable businesses.

For large merchants, the advantage of cane lay precisely in the length of its growing season. The year-long delay between planting and harvesting forced farmers to enter into debt by selling the crop in advance, to provide funds for tax payments and other needs. For merchants, a significant part of whose profit came from the supply of credit (as we will explore further in the next chapter), the longer the growing season, the greater the potential profit.
For the same reason, most farmers avoided planting sugar, due to ‘the advances that its cultivation requires’.

zh: 扩大棉花和甘蔗种植，与尼罗河洪水退去后的生态不相容。要扩大到 1820 年代三角洲部分地区首次尝试、1860—70 年代在三角洲和中埃及扩大、并被英国殖民行政官员以及欧内斯特·卡塞尔及其合伙人等金融家设想推广到全国的范围，河流的生命如今必须被摧毁。
en: Expanding the cultivation of cotton and sugar was inconsonant with the flood-recession ecology of the Nile. To extend their production on the scale first attempted in parts of the Delta in the 1820s, expanded in the Delta and Middle Egypt in the 1860s and 1870s, and envisioned for the entire country by the British colonial administrators, and by financiers like Ernest Cassel and his partners, the life of the river now had to be destroyed.

zh: 事实上，从十九世纪早些时候起就在进行的工业作物扩张，已经开始扰乱河流的洪水脉冲。这些作物不仅与个别田地的淹没不相容，也与尼罗河整个涨落过程不相容。由于被改种棉花和甘蔗的田地

不再能在夏季储存大量洪水，这些作物种植的扩大使可供应对多余洪水的围堤田区减少。越来越多的洪水不得不在危险状态下被限制在河岸和运河之内。这一变化增加了尼罗河洪峰高的年份发生灾难的风险。此外，在围堤田区中，水位上涨时土地通常处于休耕状态，因此意外的淹没对作物损害不大；而河岸高地的任何淹没，通常也会因多一层淤泥而使下一季产量增加作为补偿。但当强洪水或削弱的堤坝导致棉田或甘蔗田意外被淹时，耕作者会失去整整一年的收成。
反过来，与高粱不同，工业作物不适应缺水或干旱，因此尼罗河水位低造成损失的风险要大得多。尼罗河洪水水位的周期性极端变化，以及偶尔发生意外淹没的风险，成为一种无法驾驭的威胁。英国人力图克服的所谓自然不可预测性和饥荒风险，其实是放弃更复杂的蓄水系统、引入资本化所需的脆弱控制和耐久形式的产物。
en: In fact, the expansion of industrial crops, under way from earlier in the nineteenth century, had already begun to disrupt the river’s flood pulse. The crops were incompatible not just with the flooding of individual fields, but with the entire ebb and flow of the Nile. Since the fields

that were being converted to cotton and cane were no longer able to store significant flood waters in the summer, the expanding cultivation of these crops left fewer basins available to cope with excess water. More and more of the flood had to be contained dangerously within the banks of the river and its canals. This change increased the risk of devastation in years of a high Nile crest. Moreover, with flood basins the land was usually lying fallow as the waters rose, so an unexpected inundation did little damage to crops, and any flooding of the berms was usually compensated by an increased yield in the following season thanks to the additional layer of silt. But when strong floods or weakened dykes led to the accidental flooding of a field of cotton or sugar cane, the cultivator lost an entire year’s production.

Conversely, unlike sorghum, the industrial crops were not adapted to deal with water scarcity or drought, so the risk of losses from a low Nile was much greater. The periodic extremes in the level of the Nile flood, and the occasional risk of accidental flooding, became an unmanageable threat. The apparent unpredictability of nature and risk of famine that the British sought to overcome was a product of abandoning a more complex system of water storage and of introducing the vulnerable form of control and durability required for capitalisation.

zh: 工业作物的传播也是英国人力图解决的另一个问题的原因：
即强制劳动的广泛使用和日益苛刻。十九世纪后期的
并不是欧洲人常描绘的那种专制政府部署劳动力的古老方法。
长期以来一直存在要求集体劳动维护堤岸、运河和其他灌溉工程的做法，而在帝国扩张时期，会动员规模大得多的劳动力来修建新的围堤田区和运河（通常从河流废弃的河道挖成）。
控制大庄园的包税人，以及穆罕默德·阿里治下取代他们的“税收担保人”，可以强迫他们所征税的人劳动。
但在仲夏洪水上涨时维护河岸，让水依次流入田地，然后在冬季运河干涸时清理运河，与围绕棉田和甘蔗田保持堤岸完好、把运河当作长期水库并必须不惜一切代价防止其崩溃和淹没邻近田地的工作相比，是一项易于管理的任务。
en: The spread of industrial crops was also the cause of the other problem the British sought to solve: the widespread and increasingly exacting use of the
or forced labour. The
of the later nineteenth century was not an ancient method of deploying labour by a despotic government, as the Europeans often portrayed it.

There was a longstanding practice of requiring collective labour to maintain embankments, canals, and other irrigation works, and much larger workforces were mobilised in periods of imperial expansion to construct new basins and canals (usually dug from abandoned channels of the river).
Tax farmers who controlled large estates, and the ‘tax guarantors’ who replaced them under Muhammad Ali, could compel labour from those they taxed.

But maintaining the banks as the flood water rose in midsummer and allowing it to flow into the fields in sequence, then cleaning the canals when dry in the winter, was a manageable task compared with the work of keeping the embankments intact around fields of cotton and sugar, using the canals as long-term reservoirs that had to be prevented at all costs from collapsing and flooding the adjacent fields.

zh: 英国人在把大片土地改种棉花和甘蔗时遇到的更大问题是，随着拦河堰和永久运河的发展，过去由洪水
携带并沉积在田地各处的肥沃淤泥——估计每年 1.25 亿吨——如今沉积在灌溉运河中。
田地肥力的古老来源变成了一种废物。英国占领埃及时，此时大部分
劳动力都需要用于每年挖掘这种不受欢迎的淤泥（此外还在劳动密集的棉花收获季在大庄园从事无偿劳动）。由于不可能清除这么多淤泥，主要运河的河床升高，抬高了它们从河中取水的水位，使运河在洪水低的年份更难使用，从而大大增加了这些年份耕作的风险。
en: A larger problem that the British encountered with the conversion of large tracts to cotton and sugar cane was that with the development of barrages and permanent canals the fertilising silt that used to be carried
by the flood waters and deposited across the fields – estimated at 125 million tons per year – was now deposited in the irrigation canals.
The ancient source of the fecundity of the fields had been transformed into a waste product. When the British occupied Egypt, the bulk of the

labour by that point was required for the annual excavation of this unwanted silt (and in addition as unpaid work on large estates in the labour-intensive cotton harvest). Since it was impossible to remove so much silt, the floor level of the main canals rose, raising the level at which they took water from the river and making it more difficult to use the canals in years of low floods and thus rendering the risks to cultivation in such years much greater.

zh: 横跨尼罗河的水坝
en: Dams Across the Nile

zh: 解决“废物”问题的办法，是通过在阿斯旺修建大坝、在下游以及后来在阿斯旺上游修建更多拦河堰来阻断水流，从而完成对河流的摧毁。洪水脉冲被取代：在旧河床中工程化出一条全年有水的河道，它变成一条受调控的、渠道化的水流，其中大部分甚至从未到达海洋。虽然第一座阿斯旺大坝设计了底部泄水闸，以便夏季让一些含沙水流向下游，但大部分“废物”如今会被截留在坝后水库中。拦河堰会抬高河流水位，消除每年挖运河的大部分需要。河流及其运河取代了田地和地下水库，成为本地的蓄水场所。
en: The solution to the problem of ‘waste’ was to complete the destruction of the river by building the dam at Aswan and additional barrages downstream and later upstream of Aswan to block its flow. The flood pulse was replaced by engineering a year-round channel of water in the old riverbed, which became a regulated, canalised stream, most of it never even reaching the sea. Although the first Aswan Dam was designed with under-sluices to allow some of the silt-laden water to flow downstream in the summer, much of the ‘waste’ would now be trapped in the reservoirs behind the dams. The barrages would raise the level of the river, eliminating most of the annual need to dig out the canals. The river and its canals replaced the fields and underground reservoirs as local sites of water storage.

zh: 这带来了始料未及的后果，其中几项已在描述旧地下蓄水系统优势时提到：全年抬高河流和运河水位造成盐碱化和渍水问题；常年有水的运河为寄生虫提供了栖息地，这些寄生虫引起地方性、使人衰弱的疾病；最重要的是，减少并最终消除洪水，摧毁了田地肥力和河流生物丰度所依赖的洪水脉冲。此外，在围堤田区播种的作物不需要犁地或耙地，而如今土地要接受大量机械处理——以棉花为例，至少犁三遍，把未耗尽养分的土壤翻到表面并清除杂草。
正如我们现在所知，犁地破坏土壤结构和微生物生命，逐渐降低其
肥力（也会释放植物固存的大气碳）。
所有这些因素都促成了 1900 年至 1920 年间农业产量下降 20%。农民被迫以越来越高的成本从其他来源补充流失的养分，主要是进口硝酸盐和后来的合成肥料，但未能遏止产量下降。
en: This had unforeseen consequences, several of which have already been mentioned in describing the advantages of the old system of underground water storage: raising the water level of the river and canals year-round caused problems of salination and water logging; perennial canals provided a home for parasites that caused endemic and debilitating diseases; and, above all, reducing and eventually eliminating the flood destroyed the flood pulse on which both the fertility of the fields and the richness of the river’s biota depended. In addition, while crops sown in flood basins required no ploughing or harrowing, the land now received extensive mechanical treatment – a minimum of three ploughings in the case of cotton, to bring unexhausted soil to the surface and eliminate weeds.
Ploughing, as we now know, destroys the structure and microbial life of the soil, gradually reducing its
fertility (and also releases the atmospheric carbon sequestered by plants).

All of these factors contributed to the 20 per cent decline in agricultural yields between 1900 and 1920. Farmers were forced to replace the lost nutrients from other sources, mainly imports of nitrates and later of synthetic fertiliser, at an increasing cost, but failed to stem the decline in yields.

zh: 河流被毁的又一个代价——对资本化而言则是好处——是它的洪泛平原不仅变得更不肥沃，而且可以改作道路和住房用地。此前，人类定居主要局限于今河道及古代废弃河道两岸抬高的天然堤；河谷边缘未开垦的陡崖；以及众多高出洪泛平原的“土丘”（tell），即人类聚居形成的土墩，是在同一地点建造和重建数百年甚至数千年的结果。随着洪水被消除，富裕者如今可以把住房扩展到村镇下方的田地中，或在乡间建造豪华的
（庄园），包括约瑟夫·熊彼特参与规划的开罗以北那座庄园。
此外，在开罗和其他城市周围，土地开发公司开始把现有和潜在的农田改造成投机性住房项目，以及制砖厂和其他工业设施。因此，农田不仅变得更不肥沃，也变得更不可得，尽管有人许诺洪水控制会扩大耕种面积。相反，在大坝建成后的几年里，耕地面积实际上减少了。
甚至 1960 年代规模大得多的阿斯旺高坝，在建成后的十年里也没有带来耕地面积的增加，主要原因是城市侵占。
然而，所有这些土地损失都无法与努比亚人所遭受的损失相比；努比亚是阿斯旺以南尼罗河瀑布群之间的地区。第一座阿斯旺大坝的修建淹没了他们土地的最北一百英里，而 1933 年大坝加高又淹没了整个上努比亚。后来的高坝形成了水库，把这个地区——田地和村庄——整个抹去了。
en: A further cost of the river’s destruction, and benefit for capitalisation, was that its floodplain was rendered not only less fertile, but available for conversion to roadways and housing. Human settlement had previously been confined mainly to the raised berms along the banks of the current river channel and of ancient, abandoned channels; to the uncultivated escarpment at the valley’s edge; and to the numerous ‘tells’ or human-formed settlement mounds rising above the floodplain, the result of building and rebuilding for centuries or millennia on the same site. With the elimination of the flood, the well-to-do could now expand their housing into the fields below the villages and towns, or build lavish
, or estates, in the countryside, including the estate that Joseph Schumpeter took a hand in planning, north of Cairo.

In addition, around Cairo and other cities, land development companies began converting both existing and potential farmland into speculative housing schemes, and into factories for brick-making and other industries. So agricultural land became not only less fertile but less available, despite the promise that flood control would extend the area of cultivation. Instead, the cultivated area actually decreased in the years after the building of the dam.
Even the much larger High Dam, in the 1960s, produced no increase in cultivated area in the decade after it was built, due largely to urban encroachment.

None of that loss of land, however, compared with the loss suffered by the people of Nubia, the country lying between the Nile cataracts south of Aswan. The building of the first Aswan Dam flooded the northernmost hundred miles of their land, while the raising of the dam in 1933 submerged all of Upper Nubia. The High Dam was later to form a reservoir that obliterated the entire country – fields and villages alike.
body.review: 校注：底本把1933年大坝加高的淹没区域写为“上努比亚”，并笼统称后来的水库抹去整个地区。密歇根大学凯尔西博物馆对阿斯旺坝及淹没遗址的介绍使用“下努比亚”。此处应注意上下努比亚及实际淹没范围的区别；正文保留原作表述。 https://exhibitions.kelsey.lsa.umich.edu/galleries/Exhibits/AncientNubia/PhotoIntro.html

zh: 最后，终止洪水不仅终结了一种耕作制度，也终结了塑造埃及本身的地质过程。每年冲积物的沉积形成了三角洲——如今大多数埃及人在那里生活和耕作——并把海岸线作为宽阔的扇形向地中海延伸。几千年来，每年增加几毫米的尼罗河沉积物挡住了大海，并抵消了三角洲的逐渐下沉；这种下沉

是由下方地层的压实造成的。失去洪水之后，土地继续下沉，而二十世纪后期以来的全球变暖又使海平面稳步上升，这一改造地球的过程被推向反面。到二十一世纪初，每年有数十米海岸线被大海夺去。混凝土海防设施可以限制部分地表损失，却无法阻止海水渗入下方地下水。三角洲北三分之一的地下水变成咸水，越来越无法支撑农业；中间三分之一的地下水变成半咸水，对大多数作物有害。尼罗河变成一个大半封闭的水库，只有不到 10% 的水到达地中海，大海如今正在使土地盐碱化。所有这一切，甚至发生在全球持续变暖将带来的更大海平面上升之前。
en: Finally, ending the flood brought to an end not just a system of farming but the geological process through which Egypt itself had been formed. The annual deposit of alluvium had formed the Delta where the majority of Egyptians now lived and farmed, building out its shoreline as a wide fan into the Mediterranean. Over millennia, the annual increment of a few millimetres of Nile sediment had kept the sea at bay and counteracted the gradual sinking of the Delta, a phenomenon

caused by the compaction of the strata beneath. Deprived of the flood, with the land continuing to sink, and with global warming from the late twentieth century causing the sea level steadily to rise, this terraforming process was pushed into reverse. By the early twenty-first century, dozens of metres of coastline were being lost to the sea each year. Concrete sea defences could limit some of the surface loss but could not prevent the sea’s infiltration of the groundwaters below. The groundwater of the northern third of the Delta turned saline, increasingly unable to support agriculture, and that of the middle third became brackish, rendering it harmful to most crops. With the Nile turned into a largely enclosed reservoir, less than 10 per cent of its water reaching the Mediterranean, the sea was now salting the earth. All this was occurring even before the much larger rise in sea levels that continued global warming would bring.

zh: 洪水脉冲的逐渐消除，伴随着产权和土地税的转变。在十九世纪重新工程化尼罗河之前，开罗政府征收农业税，每年根据哪些土地被淹、种植什么作物进行调整。在中世纪，种植小麦、亚麻等的土地有不同的税类，而前一年种植过这些作物或其他耗尽土壤肥力的作物的土地也有不同税类。这些土地会以不同方式评估，以允许休耕期，或种植能恢复土地肥力的作物。虽然税收不是按产量的百分比征收，但仍根据肥力、洪水脉冲和作物性质的变化进行校准。十九世纪，政府在包税制时期之后恢复直接征税时，取消了税收、作物与土壤肥力之间的这种关系。
en: The gradual elimination of the flood pulse was accompanied by a transformation in property rights and land taxes. Prior to the re-engineering of the Nile in the nineteenth century, governments in Cairo imposed taxes on agriculture that were adjusted each year according to variations in which lands were flooded and what crops were planted. In the medieval period, there were different tax categories for land planted with wheat, flax, and so on, but also for land planted the previous year with those or other crops that exhausted the soil. These would be assessed differently to allow periods of fallowing, or planting with crops that restored the land’s fertility. While the tax was not charged as a percentage of the yield, it was calibrated nevertheless to the variation in fertility, flood pulse, and the nature of the crop. In the nineteenth century, when the government restored direct taxation after the period of subcontracted tax farming, it eliminated this relation between tax payments, crops and soil fertility.

zh: 与上一代人修建的苏伊士运河一样，大坝本身也是一个具有耐久性——延展的时间和工程尺度——的项目，这使它可供资本化。尺度之所以重要，不是因为它产生更高效或更有效的灌溉机制，而是因为它创造一台耐久的信用机器。它建造了信用创造所需的未来。
en: Like the Suez Canal a generation earlier, the dam itself was a project with a durability – an extended temporal and technical scale – that made it available to capitalisation. Scale matters, not because it produces a more efficient or effective irrigation mechanism, but because it creates a durable credit machine. It builds the future that the creation of credit requires.

zh: 自 1876 年债务危机以来，埃及的公共财政一直处于一名英国和一名法国控制者的监督之下。代表私人欧洲债权人的机构公共债务基金（Caisse de la Dette publique）直接接收政府收入，包括关税、铁路和电报收入，以及其他指定用于偿债的来源。该基金实际上作为一家私人经营的国库运作。这一安排限制政府未经该基金批准
借款。尤其是法国债券持有人，拒绝批准大规模新贷款，包括为修建主要灌溉工程提供资金的贷款。
en: Since the debt crisis in 1876, Egypt’s public finances were under the supervision of a British and French controller. An agency representing private European creditors, the Caisse de la Dette publique (Fund for the Public Debt), received government revenues directly, including customs duties and railway and telegraph revenues, and other sources allocated to debt service. The Caisse operated in effect as a privately run treasury. The arrangement restricted the government from borrowing
funds without the approval of the Caisse. The French bondholders, in particular, refused to approve large new loans, including a loan to finance the building of major irrigation works.

zh: 阿斯旺大坝的融资不是通过政府直接借款，而是通过在伦敦货币市场创造货币。英国金融家欧内斯特·卡塞尔设计了一个不同寻常的投资方案来支付大坝费用。这不仅是关于大坝如何获得融资、一项大型工程如何找到信用供给的问题，更是关于金融
、大规模信用的创造如何找到一种使其得以产生的物质结构的问题。
en: The Aswan Dam was financed, not by direct government borrowing, but by creating money on the London money markets. Ernest Cassel, the British financier, created an unusual investment scheme to pay for the dam. This is not just a question of how the dam was financed, how a large engineering work found a supply of credit, but more, how finance
, how the creation of large-scale credit found a material structure through which it could come into being.

zh: 大坝施工合同授予一家英国工程公司。工程款不是以现金支付，而是以“灌溉凭证”支付。这是一种由卡塞尔及其合伙人创造的货币形式；他们在伦敦成立了灌溉投资公司，并通过英格兰银行发行这些凭证。投资者分期购买面值 100 英镑的凭证，从其银行账户开出支票，先支付 5 英镑的初始支票，再加上 3 英镑的费用，使凭证总成本达到 103 英镑。这一切都不涉及支付过去储蓄的资金：它由埃及农民未来的税款提供资金。购买股份的投资者的银行通过把每笔支票付款记作投资者的借方、并把相同金额记入英格兰银行贷方，创造出信用货币。后者反过来在施工各阶段完成后，用三年时间把资金记入承包商账户的贷方。与此同时，埃及政府本应对通过新蓄水系统获得灌溉水的土地增税；然而，如前所述，获得灌溉的土地面积——因而税收的增加——远低于大坝支持者的预期，而且土地产量开始急剧下降。三年后，埃及政府开始每半年从这些税收中向凭证持有人的银行账户付款，通过卡塞尔转交，并附加相当于约 6% 利率的额外金额。利息的三分之二归凭证持有人，三分之一归卡塞尔及其合伙人。为了组织一笔 270 万英镑的贷款——其中没有他本人的任何资本——作为项目企业家的卡塞尔赚取了估计 50 万至 100 万英镑的费用。大坝是一台攫取远不止灌溉水的机器。
en: The contract for the construction of the dam was awarded to a British engineering firm. The work was paid not in cash but in ‘irrigation certificates’. This was a form of money created by Cassel and his partners, who set up the Irrigation Investment Corporation in London and issued the certificates through the Bank of England. Investors purchased £100 certificates in instalments, by writing cheques on their bank accounts, starting with an initial cheque for £5, with a £3 fee bringing the total cost of the certificate to £103. None of this involved the payment of funds saved from the past: it was funded by the future tax payments of Egyptian farmers. The banks of the investors buying shares created credit money, by marking each cheque payment as a debit against the name of the investor and crediting the same amount to the Bank of England. The latter, in turn, credited the funds to the contractor’s account, over three years, as the stages of construction were completed. Meanwhile, the Egyptian government was supposed to increase the tax on lands that received irrigation waters via the new storage system, although, as noted, the areas of land irrigated, and thus the increase in taxes, were much less than the dam’s proponents had anticipated, and yields from the land began a sharp decline. After three years, the Egyptian government began making payments every six months from these tax revenues to bank accounts of the holders of the certificates, through Cassel, with an additional amount equivalent to an interest rate of about 6 per cent. Two-thirds of the interest went to the certificate holders, and one-third to Cassel and his partners. For organising a loan of £2.7 million, in which none of his own capital was involved, Cassel, the entrepreneur of the project, earned a fee estimated at £500,000 to £1 million. The dam was a machine for capturing much more than irrigation waters.

zh: 这笔惊人的交易只是开始。卡塞尔及其合伙人在

阿斯旺大坝下游不远的康翁波平原投资建立了甘蔗种植园。该方案吸引数百名小投资者和佃农，他们难以获得回报或维持生计。卡塞尔还成立了一个银行财团，命名为埃及国民银行，以向埃及政府提供更多信贷。在大坝修建宣布之前，卡塞尔设计了一套同样复杂的安排，以收购前赫迪夫的那些被称为达伊拉·萨尼亚（Daira Saniya）或王室领地的大片糖业种植园——拥有二十二座榨糖厂——以及棉花庄园，它们已被抵押给他的欧洲债权人。大坝的修建急剧提高了这些地产的价值。其中一些以巨额利润转手，而购买它们的初始信用同样是由相关金融家创造的。工业设备以及部分糖业地产由卡塞尔保留，他与欧内斯特·克罗尼耶和当地投资者合伙，创建了埃及糖业公司——正如我们在上一章所见，约瑟夫·熊彼特的企业家理论正是在那里诞生的。
en: This astounding deal was just the start. Cassel and his partners invested in the creation of a sugar plantation on the Plain of Kom Ombo,

just downstream from the dam at Aswan. The scheme drew in hundreds of small investors and tenant farmers, who struggled to make a return or a living. Cassel also set up a banking consortium, which he named the National Bank of Egypt, to extend further credit to the Egyptian government. Before the building of the dam was announced, Cassel engineered an equally intricate arrangement to acquire the former Khedive’s sugar plantations, the vast landholdings known as the Daira Saniya, or royal domain, with twenty-two cane-pressing mills, and cotton estates, which had been mortgaged to his European creditors. The construction of the dam sharply increased the value of the estates. Some of these were turned over at large profit, again with the credit for their initial purchase created by the financiers involved. The industrial plant and some of the sugar estates were retained by Cassel, in partnership with Ernest Cronier and local investors, who created the Egyptian Sugar Company – the place, as we saw in the last chapter, where Joseph Schumpeter’s theory of the entrepreneur was born.

zh: 此后，几十名、最终几百名企业家开始意识到糖业和棉花庄园的资本化机会。欧洲人有时与开罗当地合伙人一起，成立土地投资公司。这些公司会取得边缘土地的所有权，这些土地如今可以被平整、灌溉，并出租给耕作者。资本化按十四年计算：土地如今可以出售，但不是按过去地块易手的旧价格（与土地税水平相关），而是（如同给公司股份估值的新方法一样）按照一种新颖的计算机制：其价值基于预期未来收益，为年净利的十四倍。
地价和地租几乎一夜之间翻了一番。但为了得到这个价格，一半土地必须种上棉花。棉花需要三年轮作，以防土壤迅速枯竭。由于资本化建立在让一半而非三分之一的土地种棉花的基础上，土壤枯竭加速，产量开始急剧下降。
en: Following this, dozens and eventually hundreds of other entrepreneurs began to realise the opportunities for the capitalisation of sugar and cotton estates. Europeans, sometimes with local Cairo partners, set up land investment companies. These would acquire title to marginal lands that could now be levelled, irrigated, and leased to cultivators. Capitalisation was calculated over fourteen years: land could now be sold, not at the old rates at which parcels changed hand, related to levels of land tax, but (as with the new method of valuing company shares) according to a novel mechanism of calculation: its value was based on estimated future earnings, at fourteen times the annual net profit.

Land prices and rents doubled almost overnight. But, to obtain this price, half the land had to be planted in cotton. Cotton requires a three-year rotation, to prevent rapid depletion of the soil. With capitalisation based on keeping half rather than one-third of the land in cotton, soil depletion accelerated and yields began their sharp decline.

zh: 土地开发
en: Land Development

zh: 与此同时，更大规模的未来可以建立在尼罗河大坝所许诺的未来之上。这个结构不仅工程化了资本化农业的新可能性；它还第一次暗示，英国占领有着长期的未来，而正是这一占领批准并促成了大坝的建设。这个预期的政治未来，为

其他长期结构提供了框架。随着房地产开发公司成立，在开罗建设新街区，以及像马阿迪和赫利奥波利斯这样的整个郊区——通常与给开发商的垄断特许权相结合，以经营电车和公用事业——出现了城市土地繁荣。“根据 1914 年的数字，在 2.1 亿埃及镑（埃及外国资本投资总额）中，1.663 亿镑，即 79%，属于非生产性投资（公共债务、抵押贷款和银行）；2,650 万镑，即 12.6%，属于运输和贸易；只有 1,050 万镑，即仅仅 5%，属于工业和建筑。”
en: Meanwhile, much larger futures could be built on the future promised by the dam. The structure engineered not just new possibilities for capitalised agriculture; it implied, for the first time, a long-term future for the British occupation that sanctioned and facilitated the dam’s construction. The projected political future provided the frame for

other long-term structures. There was an urban land boom, as property development companies were formed to build new neighbourhoods in Cairo, and entire suburbs like Maadi and Heliopolis, typically built in association with monopoly concessions to developers to run tramways and utilities. ‘According to the figures given for 1914, out of £E210,000,000 (the total sum of foreign capital investments in Egypt), 166,300,000 or 79 per cent was accounted for by non-productive investments (public debt, mortgage and banks), 26,500,000, or 12.6 per cent, by transport and trade and only 10,500,000 or a mere 5 per cent by industry and construction.’

zh: 请注意，资本化的权力不必掌握在私人手中。完全可以把未来支付的非凡意外之财转化为公共收入，用于社会目的。最初在某些情况下，事情就是这样发生的。例如，埃及干线铁路从 1850 年代开始由政府修建。统治政权拒绝把权利授予私人公司。到 1904 年，铁路占政府收入的 20%——尽管政府因 1870 年代的债务危机不得不把这些收入用于偿债。
en: Note that the powers of capitalisation did not have to be placed in private hands. It would have been perfectly possible to convert the extraordinary windfalls from future payments into public revenue and use them for social ends. Initially, in some cases, this happened. For example, the mainline Egyptian railways, starting in the 1850s, were built by the government. The ruling regime refused to grant the rights to private companies. By 1904, the railways were responsible for 20 per cent of government revenue – although it had been forced by the 1870s debt crisis to commit those revenues to the repayment of debt.

zh: 资本如何消费未来？我们又如何对此视而不见？对未来的消费看起来是投机性的、脆弱的、人造的。但事实上，它通过一套必须被工程化的攫取技术装置运作。这种工程化使资本家和殖民者——正如我们在埃及案例中所探讨的——能够把从未来攫取的收入描绘成技术进步的产物，而不是那些日后以自己的生活偿还这笔收入的人所创造的产物。我们已在运河、蓄水系统、动物和作物的层面上仔细研究了这种工程化，因为技术进步和经济进步的主张对我们的想象力有如此强大的控制力——强大到我们甚至不再听见水车曾经如何吱呀作响。这种工程化不一定带来财富或福祉的改善——事实上，它可能使两者恶化。它的设计主要是为了改善对未来的攫取。
en: How does capital consume the future? And how are we made blind to this? The consumption of the future appears speculative, flimsy, and artificial. But, in fact, it works through a technical apparatus of capture, which must be engineered. This engineering allows the capitalist, and the coloniser, as we have explored in the case of Egypt, to portray the revenue captured from the future as the product, not of those whose lives later on repay it, but of technical improvements. We have studied the engineering closely, at the level of canals, storage systems, animals, and crops, for the claim of technical improvement and economic progress has such a hold on our imagination – a hold so powerful that we no longer even hear how the waterwheel used to squeak. The engineering does not necessarily produce any improvement in wealth or well-being – in fact, it can make those worse. It was designed mainly to improve the capture of the future.
